items.title: All the latest updates on AI data centers
items.description:
Massive new data centers are the physical foundation for tech companies’ hopes and dreams for AI. But the rush to expand warehouses full of energy-hungry servers has also kicked up fights across the world over their impact on power grids, utility bills, nearby communities, and the environment.
Data centers were a major bipartisan issue ahead of the 2026 midterms, and voters largely opposed data center expansion at the polls. Tech giants like OpenAI and Amazon are promising to work more closely with local communities and cover their data center energy costs. But following the election, Democratic leaders are calling for further data center restrictions and slowdowns that the AI companies will have to grapple with.

items.descriptionZh:
大规模新建数据中心被视为科技公司实现人工智能愿景的物理基础，但其快速扩张正在全球范围内引发围绕电网负荷、居民电费、邻近社区和环境影响的多方冲突。数据中心已成为2026年美国中期选举前的重要两党议题，选民在投票中普遍反对数据中心扩张。OpenAI、亚马逊等科技巨头承诺加强与当地社区合作，并承担数据中心的能源成本。但选举结束后，民主党领导人呼吁对数据中心实施进一步限制和放缓建设，这将成为AI企业必须应对的政策压力。

从技术上看，数据中心是集中部署大量高能耗服务器、为AI模型训练和推理以及云计算提供算力的基础设施。原文并未展开具体芯片、冷却、供电架构或能效技术细节，也未给出具体性能参数和对比数据，报道重点在于数据中心扩张带来的社会、政治和环境后果。其所谓“创新点”更多体现在企业应对方式上，例如承诺与社区更紧密协商、承担能源成本等，而非某项具体工程技术突破。

技术影响方面，AI算力需求增长将使数据中心成为电力系统和土地利用的重要压力来源，可能推高电网升级需求、引发电价公平争议，并带来环境许可和社区接受度问题。应用场景主要是大模型训练与推理、云服务及AI基础设施支撑。The Verge的报道范围涵盖太空数据中心等大胆计划、各地数据中心建设的激烈地方争斗以及潜在环境影响。整体来看，AI公司正面临越来越强的监管和社区阻力，算力扩张不再只是技术问题，而是能源、环境与政治治理问题。

items.content: inMusic, the parent company of Akai, Moog, Native Instruments, and more, has decided to embrace the modding community. In an interview with The Verge, inMusic CEO Jack O’Donnell said, “We’re going to provide a toolbox to the community, we’re going to provide the inner workings of, say, an MPC or Sample so that people can do what they want.” That “toolbox” includes making the code for devices like the recently teased MPC Sample Key open source, but also offering developers an SDK to make modifications easier and lessen the risk of bricking your beloved sampler.While Akai is eager to see what the modding community cooks up, and has started seeding devices to developers ahead of the official release of the Sample Key, the company takes reliability seriously. O’Donnell said the company wants to “make sure that our official software is completely stable and good for an artist on stage.” He can’t have Fred Again going on stage and discovering his MPC is riddled with bugs. But he also wants people to feel comfortable tinkering. “We’ll try to give them a reset button,” he said so “They can experiment with it, and then not lose what they have.”The company is planning to make a big splash NAMM, the annual convention of music manufacturers in Anaheim, with Creator Lab, where it will let technically curious musicians get some hands-on time hacking 22 new products from across its brands. That includes products from Moog, that might not seem like a natural pairing for vibe coding because of its analog design. But O’Donnell thinks it can be, “if we open it up correctly.” That will involve building a platform for devs to work around the analog parts of the circuit.Other companies have also embraced the modding community. Erica Synths recently released the source code for its LXR-02 drum machine, Polyend open-sourced its line of Tracker grooveboxes, and Behringer has also announced a slew of open-source devices, including a $150 clone of the MPC One called Kick, a clone of the E-mu SP-1200, the Anima DJ controller, the Ignite sequencer, and the Polykeys 61 MIDI controller.The change in the industry has been quick and seismic. O’Donnell said of the need to provide developers tools for hacking inMusic’s products, “I can tell you it wasn’t on our task list five weeks ago. It just all of a sudden has to be on a task list now.”Of course, not everyone is thrilled. Elektron has expressed mixed feelings about the emergence of vibe-coded mods. The company banned linking to hacks and modified firmware from its official forums, though not discussing them generally, citing concerns about the possibility of damaging instruments. A statement posted on its forums says: “We would always warn against modifications to our firmware and/or machines that could brick them (potentially rendering them unusable), prevent future updates, affect warranty coverage.”While Elektron doesn’t want people posting links to hacked Digitone firmware on its forums, it’s not actively trying to thwart the modding community. The consensus is there’s no going back now that vibe coding has upended the music gear world, and trying to stand in the way would be a mistake. inMusic’s O’Donnell told the Verge, “you can try to wall them off, which is just a losing battle one … and so we want to embrace them.”

items.titleZh: How Akai and Moog are embracing vibe-coded mods
items.descriptionZh:
inMusic——Akai、Moog、Native Instruments等音乐设备品牌的母公司——正在转向拥抱硬件改装与开源社区。该公司CEO Jack O’Donnell在接受The Verge采访时表示，inMusic计划向社区提供“工具箱”，开放MPC、Sample等设备的内部运作信息，让用户按自己的需求进行修改。具体措施包括将近期预告的MPC Sample Key等设备的代码开源，并向开发者提供SDK，以降低改装门槛和设备“变砖”的风险。Akai一方面希望看到改装社区做出新东西，并已在Sample Key正式发布前向开发者发放设备；另一方面仍强调可靠性，称必须确保官方软件对舞台艺人完全稳定，不能让艺人在演出时遇到满身bug的MPC。为此，公司计划提供“重置按钮”式恢复机制，让用户放心实验而不丢失原有内容。

在技术路径上，inMusic的创新不在于单一性能参数，而在于把原本封闭的音乐硬件固件、应用层和开发接口部分开放给社区，并通过SDK和恢复机制在“可改装”与“可演出”之间建立平衡。公司还计划在阿纳海姆举行的NAMM展会期间推出Creator Lab，让对技术感兴趣的音乐人亲手hack其跨品牌22款新品，其中包括Moog产品。Moog以模拟电路设计著称，看似不适合社区快速实验性改装，但O’Donnell认为只要开放方式正确仍可行，并将围绕模拟电路部分为开发者构建平台。新闻未披露这些产品的具体处理器、延迟、复音数等性能指标，重点在于生态策略：用官方稳定版本服务现场演出，用开放工具服务开发者和DIY用户。

行业层面，音乐硬件开放源码和改装正在快速升温。Erica Synths已发布LXR-02鼓机源码，Polyend开源了Tracker系列groovebox，Behringer也宣布多款开源设备，包括售价150美元的MPC One克隆Kick、E-mu SP-1200克隆、Anima DJ控制器、Ignite音序器和Polykeys 61 MIDI控制器。O’Donnell称，为开发者提供改装工具“五周前还不在任务清单上”，现在却突然成为必须项，显示行业变化之快。

不过，并非所有厂商都完全欢迎。Elektron对“vibe coding”式改装表达复杂态度，禁止其官方论坛链接到破解和修改固件，但并未一般性禁止讨论，理由是担心损坏乐器。其论坛声明警告，修改固件和机器可能导致设备变砖、阻止未来更新并影响保修。尽管如此，Elektron并未积极阻挠改装社区。行业共识是，社区驱动的快速实验性改装已经搅动音乐设备世界，现在无法回头，试图筑墙阻止是错误策略。O’Donnell也表示，把用户隔离开是一场必败之战，因此inMusic选择拥抱社区。这一转向可能推动音乐硬件从封闭产品转向更开放的开发平台，影响现场演出、工作室制作、DIY改装和教育实验等场景，同时也将迫使厂商重新设计保修、安全恢复和官方/社区软件并存的规则。

items.content: A year ago, NVIDIA open sourced its Aerial wireless software, joining Sionna and a broader suite of open source tools for accelerating next-generation 6G network development. Together, they give researchers a foundation for testing ideas, comparing results and building on each other’s work — connecting simulation and AI training with experiments on real over-the-air wireless systems. Today, researchers and developers are using these tools to build 6G-ready networks that do more than just transmit data — receiving signals more effectively, keeping robots and autonomous systems connected when it matters most, and adapting in real time as devices move through the world. Over the past year, global developer adoption of NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna software has grown 10x, while NVIDIA’s open source 5G/6G tools have surpassed 1 million downloads. More than 8,000 research and academic institutions worldwide are using these platforms. The projects emerging today offer a view of how future networks could look. Each addresses a different challenge, but together point toward a broader ambition for building AI-native 6G networks that deliver connectivity, computing and sensing over a converged software-defined platform for billions of people, machines and agents. Networks That Help Robots React Faster A robot picking up an object needs to understand its surroundings and act before they change. When the AI powering that decision runs on a nearby server or in the cloud, the wireless connection becomes part of the response time. Researchers are exploring a more efficient approach called goal-oriented semantic communications. Instead of sending full images, robots transmit compact descriptions of objects, their positions and their relationships. Transmitting just as much information as needed allows robots to more quickly respond, especially in dynamic environments like workplaces and warehouses. At King’s College London, researchers connected a camera-equipped robot arm to an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin running NVIDIA Sionna, which supports both software-defined 5G network and edge AI processing. In fruit-packing and cube-stacking experiments with deliberately introduced faults, the approach reduced robot task completion time by up to 52.6% and improved task success compared with sending periodic images. In addition to quicker responses and less processing overhead, the system also proved more resilient — detecting dropped objects, recovering from unsuccessful actions and, in configurations using a digital twin, checking planned movements for potential collisions before execution. Networks That Learn to Receive Signals Better For a firefighter receiving live drone footage or a rescue team searching for a missing person, timely images can help guide urgent decisions. But interference and changing radio conditions can make wireless signals harder to decode, causing errors and retransmissions that delay information from the field. AI receivers address this challenge by learning to recover information from incoming signals more effectively. Better reception could help responders maintain a clearer, more current view of a fire scene or search area. SoftBank demonstrated this by integrating a neural receiver into NVIDIA Aerial CUDA-Accelerated RAN (ACAR) and testing it with a commercial 5G smartphone. In controlled tests with interference, the neural receiver delivered higher uplink throughput than a conventional receiver at all 15 tested settings, with a maximum gain of roughly 60%. Another way to improve reception is to teach receivers about the environments where they operate. Using NVIDIA Aerial Testbed, ETH Zurich researchers found that tuning neural receivers using local measurements reduced block error rates by more than one-third compared with selected pretrained versions. Networks That Learn When to Save Power As 6G connects more devices and supports more AI applications, managing energy demand will become increasingly important. For example, a network may need enough capacity to serve a busy stadium, but demand changes when the crowd leaves. AI can help identify when spare capacity can power down — and when it needs to come back online — so operators can reduce electricity use without dropping connections. At the University of Leeds, researchers developed a system that predicts network demand 10 minutes ahead and uses those forecasts to guide base station sleep decisions. Before powering down, it checks that neighboring active stations can continue serving affected devices and monitors for changes that require capacity to be restored. The team tested their approach using a portable, NVIDIA DGX Spark-powered 5G “network-in-a-box” alongside a digital twin for validating decisions against real wireless equipment. The result: researchers reported a 45.6% reduction in RAN power consumption relative to a full-power baseline while maintaining device connectivity. Networks That Can Be Tested Faster — Before They’re Built Before deploying a network, researchers need to know how it will perform when hundreds of devices compete for connections or radio signals run into interference. Simulating these conditions helps teams evaluate designs before committing to costly equipment and field trials. But realistic simulations can take hours, limiting how many ideas researchers can explore. The Centre Tecnològic de Telecomunicacions de Catalunya (CTTC) is accelerating that process by bringing GPU-accelerated radio channel models, running on ACAR, into CTTC’s open source 5G-LENA network simulator. These models calculate how wireless signals travel between antennas and devices — a computation that grows increasingly demanding as simulated networks grow. In an early evaluation, the approach reduced simulation runtime from approximately three hours to 10-20 minutes, depending on the integration, while preserving the expected statistical behavior and network performance. Faster simulations let researchers compare more designs, investigate more demanding scenarios and refine ideas sooner. As the industry develops 6G, this could shorten the path from a proposed innovation to a thoroughly evaluated network design — helping teams build better connectivity before deploying it in the real world. At NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C., attend 6G Developer Sessions where researchers and developers will showcase more innovations shaping the future of wireless networks. NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna are available on GitHub.

items.titleZh: NVIDIA 开源工具如何助力研究人员构建下一代 6G 网络
items.descriptionZh:
一年前，NVIDIA 将其 Aerial 无线软件开源，并与 Sionna 及更广泛的开源工具套件一起，为下一代 6G 网络研发提供加速基础。这些工具把仿真、AI 训练与真实空口无线系统实验连接起来，使研究人员能够测试想法、比较结果并在彼此工作基础上继续推进。过去一年，全球开发者对 NVIDIA AI Aerial 和 NVIDIA Sionna 软件的采用量增长 10 倍，NVIDIA 开源 5G/6G 工具下载量超过 100 万次，全球已有 8000 多家研究和学术机构使用这些平台。当前涌现的项目展示了未来网络的可能形态：它们分别解决不同挑战，但共同指向一个更广泛的目标——构建 AI 原生 6G 网络，在融合的软件定义平台上为数十亿人、机器和智能体同时提供连接、计算和感知能力。

在机器人应用方面，研究人员正在探索“目标导向语义通信”。传统方式下，机器人若依赖附近服务器或云端 AI 做决策，无线连接时延会成为响应时间的一部分；新方法不再传输完整图像，而是发送关于物体、位置及其关系的紧凑描述，只传输必要信息，从而加快动态环境中的响应速度。伦敦国王学院将配备摄像头的机械臂连接到运行 NVIDIA Sionna 的 NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin，该系统同时支持软件定义 5G 网络和边缘 AI 处理。在水果包装和方块堆叠实验中，研究人员故意引入故障，结果显示该方法将机器人任务完成时间最多缩短 52.6%，任务成功率也优于周期性发送图像的方式。系统还表现出更强韧性，可检测掉落物体、从失败动作中恢复，并在使用数字孪生的配置中于执行前检查计划运动是否可能碰撞。

在信号接收方面，AI 接收机通过学习更有效地从 incoming 信号中恢复信息，以应对干扰和无线条件变化造成的解码困难、错误和重传。软银将神经接收机集成到 NVIDIA Aerial CUDA 加速 RAN（ACAR）中，并用商用 5G 智能手机测试。在受控干扰测试中，神经接收机在全部 15 个测试设置下的上行吞吐量均高于传统接收机，最大增益约 60%。另一种思路是让接收机学习其所处环境：苏黎世联邦理工学院利用 NVIDIA Aerial Testbed 发现，使用本地测量数据调优神经接收机，相比选定的预训练版本可将块错误率降低三分之一以上。这类更佳接收能力有望帮助消防员和救援团队更清晰、更及时地获取无人机画面或搜索区域信息。

在节能方面，随着 6G 连接更多设备并支持更多 AI 应用，能耗管理将日益重要。网络需要满足体育场等场景的高容量需求，但人群离开后需求会变化。AI 可识别何时可关闭闲置容量、何时需重新上线，从而在不掉线的情况下降低用电。利兹大学开发了一套系统，可提前 10 分钟预测网络需求，并用预测指导基站休眠决策；休眠前会检查邻近活跃基站能否继续服务受影响设备，并监测需要恢复容量的变化。团队使用由 NVIDIA DGX Spark 驱动的便携式 5G“network-in-a-box”以及数字孪生，在真实无线设备上验证决策。结果显示，相对于全功率基线，RAN 功耗降低 45.6%，同时保持设备连接。

在网络仿真与部署前验证方面，研究人员需要了解数百台设备竞争连接或信号遇到干扰时的网络表现。真实感仿真可帮助团队在投入昂贵设备和现场试验前评估设计，但往往耗时数小时，限制可探索的想法数量。加泰罗尼亚电信技术中心（CTTC）将运行在 ACAR 上的 GPU 加速无线信道模型引入其开源 5G-LENA 网络仿真器。这些模型计算无线信号在天线与设备间的传播，随着仿真网络规模增大，计算需求也日益提高。早期评估显示，该方法将仿真运行时间从约 3 小时缩短至 10—20 分钟（取决于集成方式），同时保持预期的统计行为和网络性能。更快仿真使研究人员能比较更多设计、研究更苛刻场景并更早完善想法，有望缩短从提出创新到完成全面评估网络设计的路径，帮助团队在真实部署前构建更好的连接能力。

总体来看，这些项目覆盖机器人实时响应、AI 神经接收、智能节能和高效仿真验证等 6G 关键方向，体现了开源工具在连接仿真、AI 训练与真实无线实验方面的作用。NVIDIA 表示，AI Aerial 和 Sionna 已在 GitHub 上提供，并将在华盛顿特区 GTC 的 6G Developer Sessions 上展示更多塑造未来无线网络的创新。

items.title: GlobalFoundries VP details FDX Fusion technology, sporting 7nm-class performance without the need for EUV tools — company targets 2030 for high-volume manufacturing, with planar transistors in tow
items.description: GlobalFoundries reveals new details about its FDX Fusion technology, which promises 7nm-class performance and 8nm-class logic density using planar FD-SOI transistors without EUV lithography, shares what is next for FDX Fusion node, and the FDX program in general.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Eight years after GlobalFoundries abandoned the development of its 7nm FinFET technology, the company is preparing to return to 7nm-class performance, this time by going via a different route. Its FDX Fusion process, built on FD-SOI (fully depleted silicon-on-insulator) technology, promises 7nm-class performance using advanced planar transistors, with no EUV lithography necessary.In an interview with Tom's Hardware Premium, GlobalFoundries' Sudipto Bose, vice president of the FD-SOI business unit, shared new details about its FDX Fusion technology, including its 8nm-class logic density, advanced planar transistors, manufacturing costs, and plans to begin commercial production in 2028. The company also explained how it intends to compete with conventional FinFET technologies and why it believes FD-SOI has a future beyond the 22nm-class generation. Some elements of this interview transcript have been edited for flow and clarity.Sudipto Bose: I have been at GlobalFoundries (GF) for a little bit over six years, and I have been in the industry for 25+ years. I spent the rest of my career at Texas Instruments (TI), so it's really two jobs that I have done: TI and GF. Half and half engineering and business. I spent a lot of my business days in the automotive segment. This was what I was doing at GF when I joined, and now I have the FDX product line role.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Sudipto Bose: A little bit on the history of FDX at GF. GF has been investing in FD-SOI for a long time. It started [these efforts] before I joined. So I would say almost eight years now. And a lot of the investment thesis that drove us towards FDX Fusion is based on the traction that we have in the market today, right? We have quite a few customers who are ramping up. And I say quite a few; this is like high double-digit customers in the nineties that are ramping up right now.Applications for FDX Fusion Anton Shilov: What specific types of chips and devices is FDX Fusion designed for? Which application will benefit most from its capabilities? You may like GlobalFoundries unveils 7nm-class FDX Fusion node — comes 7 years after firm abandoned FinFET China crafts working 3nm gate-all-around transistors without EUV Analyzing Intel's EMIB and Foveros advanced packaging roadmaps Sudipto Bose: FDX Fusion will try to enhance the applications in which we play today. What do I mean by that? If you look at our current customers, they are designing chips, everything to do with connectivity. When I say connectivity, think of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, satcom, all of that. So that is one class of customers.There's another class of customers who are designing processors at the edge, so these are MCUs (microcontroller units) with some level of inference sitting inside. Think of customers like Alif Semiconductors. So that is another class: MCUs at the edge.Then in automotive, we have a disproportionate exposure to radar, and this is because of the eighty-one gigahertz performance that FDX brings to the table. So we will engage with them as they try to enhance their portfolio. We also have an automotive MCU, but radar is where you will see a lot of press releases that we have done.Last but not least, we also have exposure in the data center segment. This also goes back to the fT/fmax, the high-performance RF that we have, which is a good candidate for designing TIAs and clock recovery circuits. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Anton Shilov: By applications inside data centers, what exactly do you mean? CPUs? What to read next Samsung's fab roadmaps examined Intel 14A moves closer to production as PDK 0.9 becomes available The ABF substrate data center roadmap — solving the supply crunch and material wall beneath every AI accelerator Sudipto Bose: Not CPUs. It is in the connectivity space. So, if you think about GF's focus, we are very focused on two things in data centers: power and connectivity. So in the connectivity space, we have silicon photonics, or turning electrons into photons. But then when you receive them, you have the optical diode, again, a GF silicon photonics technology. After that, you need circuits that will amplify those weak electrical signals and drive them to the compute chip. This circuit, which amplifies the weak electrical signals, is right now being done by GF silicon-germanium, but once FDX Fusion is there, we'll offer them both [as] options. And so, to be very specific to your answer, these are data/signal paths inside the data center that feed into CPUs.7nm-class FD-SOI nodeGlobalFoundries' FDX Fusion is a new manufacturing technology that promises 8nm-class logic density and 7nm-class power and performance without EUV lithography or FinFET transistors, which greatly reduces design costs and manufacturing costs at the cost of significantly lower transistor density compared to 7nm-class nodes. Instead, the process relies on advanced planar fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) transistors, strained silicon substrates, and aggressive optical patterning techniques to achieve transistor dimensions comparable to those of conventional 8nm-class FinFET nodes. FDX Fusion also retains support for adaptive body biasing and combines high-density digital logic with RF, analog, and embedded memory capabilities. The technology will be manufactured using deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography, although its tighter gate and metal pitches will likely require extensive multipatterning for the most critical layers.Anton Shilov: What are the key innovations of FDX Fusion compared to predecessors and other nodes that are currently used?Sudipto Bose: The key things that we're improving from the current-generation FDX, the first one is fT/fmax, this is 500 GHz, or 0.5 THz fT/fmax. This helps the first segment that I talked about, which is connectivity. This helps automotive radar, and this definitely helps the data center segment as they try to improve data speeds. So this is not really competing with silicon germanium. Think of it as silicon germanium at the very high end, and FDX in the 100 – 200 Gb per lambda space. That is one. The second one is the inference at the edge. So we can call it physical AI, and we look at physical AI as sense, think, act, and connect. But the kind of feature set we are putting in starts with improving the digital gate density. This is 2.2 times more dense than the current generation FDX (22FDX and 22FDX+). (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Sudipto Bose: We are putting in a lot of flavors of eNVM, a lot of flavors of SRAM, because in edge AI, and in fact for any AI, the real game is how much memory you can pack without increasing the cost. So we are adding a lot of flavors of those. The way we architected FDX Fusion is that we set a goal of how much performance we can deliver to our customer base without increasing their operating expenses.If you look at classic 7nm, 6nm, they require EUV tools. The mask set is costly; the tool chain is costly. The FDX Fusion platform that we've built isn't going to use EUV tools. It is also based on planar technology. So there are two advantages to this. One is that we can support a much more competitive mask set price compared to 6nm. We can also offer [customers] a lot more flexibility in terms of cycle time and in how many places we manufacture, because FDX Fusion does not need EUV tools.So, to summarize the answer? We are trying to improve RF and analog performance, digital gate density, and the classes of memory that we offer. What applications are we trying to target? It is connectivity, edge AI, high-frequency mmWave, automotive radar, and definitely applications inside data centers. The press release says that it has more than twice the transistor density of the original 22FDX process, but you never actually published a transistor density number for this. Could you share any numbers?Sudipto Bose: I will share a number with you. But I will also give you a little bit of context on how our customers look at our technology portfolio. If you look at the current generation, the one that we are manufacturing today, the one where I said we have 90+ customers ramping. Not designing, ramping. This basically comes from the flexibility of FD-SOI. You have the box, the depleted channel, and you can use body bias. So we have customers who are able to achieve 16nm-class power and performance with 22FDX. What do I mean by 16nm-class power and performance?It essentially means that although our gate density is not as close to 16mm, when you look at the system-level requirements like CPU clock, but think of it as TOPS per watt, we are matching 16nm; in some cases, we are matching 12nm-class.[...] If I were sitting in a time machine and went back seven years, instead of calling it 22FDX, we could have called it 16FDX, right? Or we could have called it 16nm-class FDX. So with that analogy, if you come to FDX Fusion, our gate density of FDX Fusion will be exactly the same as the industry's 8nm standard today.It is 14 million gates per square millimeter; that is the density.Note: Assuming he uses a two-input NAND gate as its reference, each gate contains four transistors, which translates to 56 MTr/mm², which is comparable to what Samsung's 8nm-class nodes use.Sudipto Bose: Now, why do we call it 7nm-class? Or we actually thought of calling it 6nm-class, but then we said, let's wait for some silicon before we go too far ahead. It is because digital gate density is one aspect of a solution. It defines your physical size, the die size, and that is great. But then you need power and performance. And with the adaptive body bias (ABB) capability that FD-SOI has, and with the standard cell metallization innovations that we have brought in FDX Fusion, once a device is done and you again look at TOPS per watt, it should be equivalent, if not better, than what 7nm can achieve. That is our product target. So for a customer, the value it brings [customers] is: 'I do not have to use an EUV tool line. I do not have to use a mask set that costs many millions of dollars.'I have something which costs a few millions of dollars, has great cycle time, but at the same time, I am getting TOPS per watt, which is similar to or better than 7nm. The die size might be bigger, but again, it should not be no bigger than what 8nm is today. And that is the messaging to the industry; that is why we say 7nm-class instead of saying, 'Hey, this is 7nm density.' We are trying to reflect what our customers have told us. That in the edge world, in the physical AI world, the size of the die is one aspect, but if the die does not meet the power requirement of the application, then the whole system will not function. So that is the push.Anton Shilov: That is perhaps why you actually called the technology FDX Fusion instead of using some fancy number.Sudipto Bose: Yes, because the moment we put a number [out], people put us in a box. And we want to give customers the optionality of, 'Listen, you want to design a transimpedance amplifier using the fT/fmax that we have? That's an analog circuit. No one cares about digital gate density. Go build it.''You want to build a simple MCU, which is just SRAM and IOs? We have 14 million gates per square millimeter. Go build it.' 'You want to build a mixed-signal design like a single-chip radar, Wi-Fi, a satcom digital beamformer? Here are the few other knobs that you can turn to get the best PPA or the best system performance that you need.'That is why we chose the name Fusion; we are trying to imply [that] we give you many options. It is the combination of all the good things the world needs to design the physical AI dream that we have put in front of ourselves, like the whole stack concept of 'sense, think, act, and connect'. Let us see if it sticks. I think it is a bold move for us to go against the grain of the way the foundry industry typically names its platforms, but we feel pretty strong about it.Anton Shilov: So, you shared the gate density number, but could you maybe also share things like contacted gate pitch, metal pitch as well?Sudipto Bose: In time. The reason I mention that is there is a little bit of IP involved. We want to get the first silicon out, engage with a few customers before we publish the CPP and the M(etal) layers. […] We are pushing the limits of patterning and coloring as well as gate oxide engineering to get the best CPP and metal pitches, which will enable this level of density of gates. That is, I would say in terms of R&D dollars just at a very high level, 50% of R&D dollars is on the transistor itself because we are doing strained substrates. There are multiple techniques we are using to improve the PFET and NFET performance. The other 50% is all on CPP and metal pitches.Anton Shilov: So, are those contacted gate pitches and metal pitches comparable to conventional 7nm class FinFET process technologies?Sudipto Bose: Comparable to 8nm.Anton Shilov: When we talk about 8nm, basically speaking, there is only one company that actually produces chips using an 8nm-class technology. That is Samsung Foundry. TSMC and Intel Foundry do not have 8nm-class technologies. So I suppose that we should compare it to Samsung's 8nm node, right?Sudipto Bose: That's a fair guess.Anton Shilov: When it comes to power consumption improvements versus 22FDX and 22FDX+, how much lower power can we get using the new FDX Fusion node?Sudipto Bose: It depends on the application, but I understand your question. So if you just normalize with [iso performance and iso power], I am giving you an answer with adaptive body bias included. If you consider current-generation FDX as the base point, the goal of FDX Fusion is to get 30% higher performance and 40% lower power. Again, it is really application-driven [in] how low you can go. But if you take the standard core, our goal is to get at least a 20% improvement.Anton Shilov: What types of chips do you expect to benefit most from the FDX Fusion technology? You mentioned connectivity, edge AI, high RF, automotive radar, and connectivity applications inside data centers. What about application-specific AI accelerators, because you mentioned edge inference?Sudipto Bose: From the STAC — sense, think, act, and connect — framework point of view, let me give you an example. Think of a humanoid, or a car — major applications that need to see. It needs to see and then infer what the environment is like. So the class of chips that do this vision processing at the edge to infer the surroundings will definitely be supported with FDX Fusion. The class of chips that will hear, do voice recognition, and, from voice recognition, draw conclusions, we definitely want to support [them]. Now, at the data center right now, as I said, our play is connectivity. Just translating optical to electrical signals.If a customer wants to use a chiplet, which has a lot of memory, think of analog in-memory compute along with an inference engine, by all means we will support [such applications]. We will work with customers to see how we can play in that compute ecosystem in the data center. But in terms of pure focus, the first 10 customers that we are engaged with are either at the edge, or they are in the connectivity piece inside the data center.Note: For those of our readers who are not familiar with ABB, this is a technique that dynamically adjusts a transistor's threshold voltage by changing the voltage applied to the transistor body. Forward body bias reduces threshold voltage to improve performance, while reverse body bias increases it to reduce power leakage. This enables chips to optimize performance and power consumption according to workload requirements. ABB is one of the key advantages of the FD-SOI technology.Anton Shilov: Since you mentioned this, does FDX Fusion retain the active body biasing capabilities of its predecessors?Sudipto Bose: It is an inseparable part of the platform, yes. We will launch this platform in a way that customers can use it.New tools requiredAnton Shilov: You also mentioned makers of wafer fab equipment. Will FDX Fusion use existing manufacturing equipment at the Dresden facility, or will it require substantial investments in new lithography, deposition, etching, and metrology tools?Sudipto Bose: It will require new tools. Substantial is a relative term. If you see the amount of money being invested in semiconductors, the term 'substantial' has changed. We are going to get new tools, which is why we combined the FDX Fusion announcement event with the topping off of the Sprint expansion project. That's why we had all the luminaries from the German and the European government. There will be tool investment; we will be buying tools from the vendors. How much of it is going to be litho versus etching? Time will tell, but for sure we need new tools compared to what we have today. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Anton Shilov: But will you essentially need to completely re-equip the Dresden facility to use FDX Fusion? What percentage of the tools you have can be reused for FDX Fusion?Sudipto Bose: We can get back to you on that exact answer because I do want to give you a proper answer, rather than a high-level answer. But I will tell you where the targets are. With the front end, the transistor fabrication tool chain, my target is to reuse as much as we can.Anton Shilov: You also mentioned that you plan to begin manufacturing FDX Fusion in 2028. But does this refer to risk production, initial customer production, or high volume manufacturing?Sudipto Bose: Initial customer production.Anton Shilov: When do you expect the technology to reach mature yields and meaningful production volumes?Sudipto Bose: I will give you my target, and then the industry will define it because we are a part of a bigger ecosystem. 2030 is when we want to get to high-volume manufacturing with FDX Fusion. But again, it depends on the first applications and the first few customers. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Readiness Anton Shilov: Speaking of customers, you probably already have customers who are committed to production, haven't you?Sudipto Bose: We have customers who are committed to building a chip. Of course, we have to deliver to their specs before they go to production.Anton Shilov: I suppose the customers that you mentioned in the press release like BMW, Bosch NXP, Siemens, and Tesla, they are all plan to build chips on this technology.Sudipto Bose: […] They have been pushing us for the last few years to do something like this, and they have given us requirements. Now we are doing it, and we have to show them what we can [deliver]. So there is a lot of push that we have received from the industry, from these companies. When I say these companies, the supply chain that leads into these companies to deliver something which will work at the edge. So we are racing against time to show them something that will meet the specs.Anton Shilov: GlobalFoundries plans to release the initial FDX Fusion PDK in mid-2027. But when do you expect complete digital, analog, and RF design flows to become available from the three major EDA vendors?Sudipto Bose: Yeah. I wish I could tell you… Right now we are in discussion with all the major primes, so we are in the request for information/request for quotation (RFI/RFQ) phase, but we have started discussions with the major EDA vendors. It has been almost six to nine months now.Anton Shilov: But you do expect all the leading EDA vendors to support FDX Fusion in eight to nine months?Sudipto Bose: Of course. We are going to engage with the whole ecosystem that we have, and once [the PDK is out], we have to support a proper flow not just for chip design, but also IPs that are required and everything else around it.Anton Shilov: So how extensive will the initial FDX Fusion IP ecosystem be? Will customers have access to silicon-proven standard cell libraries, SRAM compilers, embedded non-volatile memory, interface IPs, maybe analog and radio frequency building blocks before 2028?Sudipto Bose: Yes. In the first two years, we are going to engage with pilot customers. Think of these as early adopters. We have early adopters listed, and we will design standard cell, I/Os, and SRAM [...] needed for everything, so we will have those. But then the complex IPs, like PCIe Gen 4/5 or LPDDR6 or a DisplayPort, will be dictated by the first few applications that will ramp. FDX Fusion for us is the beginning of a journey. We have been on the journey of 22FDX for almost eight years. I envision FDX Fusion to be more than that. Even on our current platforms, we keep enhancing our IP portfolio. So I expect us to be adding IPs to FDX Fusion over the next ten years. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)ARC, MIPS, and Fusion FDXAnton Shilov: GlobalFoundries also highlighted its ARC and MIPS processor IP portfolios and RISC-V expertise as part of the FDX Fusion offering. Do you plan to develop processor cores and AI accelerators specifically optimized for FDX Fusion? IPs specifically optimized for FDX Fusion? Or will you primarily port existing IP to the new process?Sudipto Bose: MIPS is an internal customer and a partner, and we will engage with them, and they will launch a platform for physical AI that is fine-tuned, in a combination of what they have and what FDX Fusion has. ARC and MIPS are key pieces of the strategy. Having an internal customer like that just enhances our development cycle by 5X because now they can start developing fast turns of test chips and give us feedback. We did not have this capability in the past. Now we do. Once they are ready, they will start announcing stuff.Anton Shilov: So essentially, you will both port the existing IPs to the new node, but also MIPS will likely develop something brand new specifically for FDX Fusion.Sudipto Bose: Yes.Costs Anton Shilov: How will the manufacturing complexity and cost per transistor of FDX Fusion compare to 22FDX+, your 12nm FinFET technology, and conventional 8nm FinFET technology?Sudipto Bose: This would be the most advanced planar transistor that the world has seen, the most advanced non-EUV-based manufacturing line that the world has seen. So, I would say significantly more complex than our current 22nm-class FD-SOI line. More complex than what we have on the 12nm FinFET line. We are working with every tool vendor that you can think of as part of this program, and we have given them the challenges. It goes back to your question about our contacted gate pitch and metal pitch. So, we have had multiple workshops with them over the last few quarters, and each one of them is proposing a tool recipe that they think will get this to a nice and solid yield. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Sudipto Bose: So, I guess the answer to your question is: firstly, it is definitely complex, and secondly, we are really using the entire ecosystem available to us to come up with tool configurations that will deliver this. All of this is going to happen in Dresden. We have to be competitive, so price is always dictated by the market. Our goal is to have a running cost that is significantly better than a 7nm or a 6nm class of design (due to planar transistors and due to lack of EUV masks). After that, we will work with our customers to figure out what makes sense. But you are right, the value that we want to bring in is, 'dear customers, you do not have the same operating expenses load, meaning the cost of tape-out is less than 6nm.'And you can do multiple tape-outs because this class of devices is not something where you can design one part and use it for 15 applications. You really need 15 devices for 15 applications. So, we definitely enable that. Then, when it comes to manufacturing cost, it is a discussion with our customers. We have various business models, but the goal is to make sure it is a win-win. At the end of the day, the lower the cost we are, the more flexibility we can provide to our customers. The non-EUV path is one of the things that was dictated by our decision that we must keep this a cost-competitive platform.Anton Shilov: So, cost-wise you want to be competitive, but it's likely comparable to 8nm.Sudipto Bose: I will have a better feel once we are complete with what we call our M-cycles inside the fab. But I would say my internal target is that we have to be better than that.The future of FDX Anton Shilov: GlobalFoundries describes upcoming technology as its 1st Generation of FDX Fusion. Does this mean that you envision subsequent generations with high transistor density and performance? Maybe you can share some preliminary targets or timelines for the next node?Sudipto Bose: We have listed quite a few innovation steps that we want to enable on this platform. The FDX Fusion definition is based on the ones we believe we are more confident that we will be able to deliver in the timeframe that we have said. We have kept a few things in the innovation lab, and they are pushing the boundaries of a few things like eNVM, EDA routing, chip folding, 2.5D integration, which, once they mature, will define what the next version of FDX Fusion will look like. I do not have a timeline for the next version of FDX Fusion, though.As we proceed through the development phase, I would say early 2028 to mid-2028 is when I expect to have a better view of when the next version will be launched. And this is also based on feedback we will get from customers. Because what we have right now is our first silicon, which is running in the lab, which we will show to customers. They will give us a lot of feedback. I am sure we will get a few things right, and at the same time, we will get a few things not so right. And that feedback, along with a few of the innovation topics I mentioned, will dictate what the next generation is going to look like. Stay tuned! (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Anton Shilov: One of the reasons why I aksed about next-generation nodes is partly because TSMC typically shares its process technology roadmaps with new nodes well before it releases early PDKs for these nodes. Given that FDX Fusion is now GF's most advanced logic process, with capabilities comparable to 8nm-class technologies (i.e., more advanced than 22FDX or bulk 12nm FinFET), how frequently does GlobalFoundries plan to introduce new process technologies, and how far in advance will it disclose its roadmap?Sudipto Bose: I would say, we are doing advanced development across the board. If you look at the work we are doing on silicon photonics, on packaging, on power transistors like GaN, RF GaN, Power GaN, these are all pretty advanced. But yes, you are right: in what the world understands as a classic, let's say, high-density process, FDX Fusion is the most advanced. We typically announce or update the industry about our roadmap every year at the GlobalFoundries Technology Symposium. Like this year at GTS, we announced FDX Fusion. So, I would say stay tuned for the GTS sessions that we have, and typically every year we do it in September or October.CEA-Leti involvement Anton Shilov: CEA-Leti describes FDX Fusion as a single-digit FD-SOI node. How closely is this new technology related to CEA-Leti's own research in 10nm and 7nm with their SOI nodes?Sudipto Bose: The platform that we have right now is the outside of the substrate engineering work that we are doing with Soitec and CEA-Leti; the rest of it is GF inherent IP at this point in time. So we are bringing in the knowledge that we have from current-generation FDX, the knowledge that we have from the work that we did in 7nm before we stopped it, the work that we have done on 12nm. So it is bringing in all the innovations across all the GF fabs to figure out what is the best that we can offer. Does it mean that we will not look at what CEA-Leti has in the future? I do not have an answer right now. But for now, FDX Fusion is a very GF innovation-driven effort. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Anton Shilov: So you did not use pre-competitive IP from CEA-Leti to develop FDX Fusion? Is it a completely internally developed node?Sudipto Bose: Correct.Anton Shilov: The press release mentions innovations in substrate engineering along with endorsements from CEA-Leti and Soitec. What exactly does that involve, and how does it improve transistor performance? What role do Soitec and CEA-Leti play in developing FDX's strained silicon substrates, and how close is this technology to mass production?Sudipto Bose: GlobalFoundries is working with CEA-Leti and Soitec under the FAMES program to develop strained silicon substrates for FDX Fusion. The goal is to improve charge carrier mobility and, consequently, transistor performance. Since FD-SOI technology relies on specialized silicon-on-insulator wafers supplied by Soitec, the three organizations are developing ways to introduce strain into these substrates and make the technology suitable for high-volume manufacturing. The approach has already demonstrated its viability in the laboratory, and the partners are now refining the manufacturing process to prepare it for commercial production.[Session ends]

items.titleZh: 格芯副总裁详解FDX Fusion技术：无需EUV工具即可实现7nm级性能——公司目标2030年大规模量产，并采用平面晶体管
items.descriptionZh:
GlobalFoundries在约八年前放弃7nm FinFET研发后，正计划以另一条技术路线重返7nm级性能：基于FD-SOI（全耗尽绝缘体上硅）的FDX Fusion工艺。该平台采用先进平面晶体管，不依赖EUV光刻，目标是在2028年进入初始客户生产、2030年实现高量产，并提供8nm级逻辑密度和7nm级功耗性能。GlobalFoundries FD-SOI业务部门副总裁Sudipto Bose在接受Tom's Hardware采访时披露了该工艺的密度、成本、IP生态、制造安排和客户进展。

背景上，GlobalFoundries长期投资FD-SOI，现有22FDX/22FDX+平台已有90多家客户处于量产爬坡阶段，覆盖连接、边缘MCU、汽车雷达和数据中心连接等。公司称，正是这些客户对边缘物理AI和低成本先进节点的需求，推动其开发FDX Fusion。BMW、Bosch、NXP、Siemens、Tesla等汽车与工业链企业过去几年持续施压并提出规格要求。GlobalFoundries还拥有ARC、MIPS和RISC-V相关处理器IP，MIPS作为内部客户和合作伙伴将推出面向物理AI的平台，以加速测试芯片和反馈循环。

核心技术原理方面，FDX Fusion不是FinFET，而是先进平面FD-SOI晶体管，保留FD-SOI的关键能力——自适应体偏置（ABB）。ABB通过调节晶体管体端电压动态改变阈值电压：正体偏置降低阈值电压以提升性能，反体偏置提高阈值电压以降低漏电，从而按负载优化功耗和性能。FDX Fusion还采用应变硅衬底、栅氧工程以及激进的光学图形化/多重曝光技术，用DUV实现更紧的栅极和金属间距。由于不使用EUV，掩膜组成本显著低于6nm/7nm，工具链和晶圆厂选择也更灵活，但关键层需要大量多重图形化。GlobalFoundries与Soitec、CEA-Leti在FAMES计划下开发应变SOI衬底，以提高载流子迁移率和晶体管性能；该衬底方案已在实验室验证可行，正在优化量产工艺。公司强调，除衬底工程合作外，FDX Fusion主要是GlobalFoundries自有IP，未使用CEA-Leti的预竞争IP。

性能参数上，FDX Fusion的逻辑密度为每平方毫米1400万门；若以二输入NAND每门4个晶体管换算，约合56 MTr/mm²，与三星8nm级工艺相当，是22FDX的2倍以上。GlobalFoundries称其接触栅间距和金属间距与8nm级相当，但不愿在首批硅出来前公布具体CPP和金属间距。与22FDX相比，在开启ABB、等性能条件下功耗可降低40%，等功耗条件下性能提升30%；标准核心目标至少提升20%。与12LP+相比，性能提升16%、功耗降低20%，密度为56对30–40 MTr/mm²。与7nm相比，在ABB开启条件下性能约高4%、功耗约低5%，但晶体管密度明显更低（56对约91.2 MTr/mm²）；与三星8LPP相比密度为56对约61.2 MTr/mm²。其fT/fmax达到500GHz，强化了射频和毫米波能力，包括81GHz汽车雷达。公司将其定位为“7nm级”而非“7nm密度”，因为边缘物理AI更看重TOPS/W、内存容量和系统功耗，芯片面积可大于7nm但不会大于8nm。

应用场景包括：Wi-Fi、蓝牙、蜂窝、卫星通信等连接芯片；带推理能力的边缘MCU；汽车雷达和汽车MCU；数据中心内的连接链路，如硅光子接收后的跨阻放大器、时钟恢复电路，而不是CPU。FDX Fusion还面向视觉处理、语音识别、单芯片雷达、卫星通信数字波束成形、混合信号设计，以及未来可能的chiplet和模拟存内计算。公司提出“感知、思考、行动、连接”的物理AI框架，首批10家合作客户集中在边缘或数据中心连接。

制造与生态方面，FDX Fusion将在德国德累斯顿生产，需要新增设备，但前端晶体管工具链尽量复用现有设备，具体复用比例未披露。工艺复杂性显著高于22FDX和12nm FinFET，公司正与多家设备商合作开发工具配方。初始客户生产目标为2028年，高量产目标为2030年；2027年中发布初始PDK。EDA方面，公司正与主要厂商进行RFI/RFQ沟通，预计完整数字、模拟和RF流程将获支持。初期IP生态包括标准单元、I/O、SRAM及多种eNVM，复杂接口IP如PCIe Gen4/5、LPDDR6、DisplayPort将由首批量产应用决定，并计划未来十年持续扩展。成本上，公司目标使运行成本显著优于7nm/6nm级设计，内部目标甚至优于8nm级；但每晶体管制造复杂性高于现有22FDX和12nm FinFET。

总体看，FDX Fusion是GlobalFoundries避开EUV和FinFET高成本路线、以FD-SOI平面工艺服务边缘AI、连接、汽车雷达和数据中心连接的战略产品。它不以最高晶体管密度竞争，而是以射频/模拟性能、ABB灵活性、较低掩膜成本和非EUV供应链为卖点。若2028年客户生产和2030年高量产按计划推进，该平台将为欧洲先进逻辑产能和物理AI边缘芯片提供一条差异化路径，但其密度仍落后于7nm FinFET，且EDA、IP和制造良率仍需验证。

items.title: Protesters storm Microsoft AI data center construction site
items.description: The protesters stormed over the walls and took over the construction site, with the Stop Dirty Data Centers coalition saying that more actions are planned across Europe.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 12 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A Microsoft data center under construction in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, has been overrun by about a hundred protesters, with some carrying placards saying, “Screw your data center.” According to Reuters, the “Stop Dirty Data Centers” coalition is planning actions across 16 countries on November 6 and 7, 2026, including Amsterdam, Dublin, Warsaw, and another Microsoft site in Denmark.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsiblePure Data Centers, which owns the Amsterdam data center, said, “We respectfully ask those on site to leave safely and engage with us in dialogue about the development and any concerns they may have.” The report also quoted Microsoft saying that it understood the strong feeling that people have and respected their right to peaceful expression but says that it does not condone any unlawful action."On 6-7 November 2026 we are taking action across Europe to say Stop Dirty Data Centres," the group's website reads. "Local communities are rising up to stop dirty data centres where they live. We will unite and exercise our democratic rights to speak out, assemble, and protest to hold elected officials to account. We’re calling for an immediate moratorium on large data centres in Europe!" A map on the site shows actions planned at 85 locations across Europe over the coming days.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The group cited a list of concerns about "the explosion of AI data centres across our towns and cities," and claims to be joining to prevent "the irreparable harms data centres pose to the wellbeing of people and planet." They cite local communities, jobs, housing shortages and rising energy bills, the climate crisis, heatwaves and water shortages, big tech undermining democracies, the mental health crisis, increased surveillance and the erosion of privacy, securitization and militarization, and a toxic supply chain as motivations.Data center opposition is one of the issues that has taken center stage in the U.S. midterm elections, with Americans overwhelmingly voting against them. It seems that resistance isn’t limited to the United States, though, as European countries take measures to limit their unlimited development. For example, Google has been hit with a criminal probe after its Finnish subsidiary, Tuike Finland Oy, allegedly destroyed 816 acres of forest without a permit. Denmark has also hit the brakes on data center grid connection requests as total applications exceed 60GW, more than eight times the country’s current peak power consumption. One Italian council also a 200% tax on data center development in agricultural land to encourage developers to reuse old industrial areas instead. You may like Local opposition blocked $68 billion worth of data center projects in the second quarter of 2026 Microsoft-backed AI data center faces backlash over alleged unpermitted gas turbines and 1.5M-gallon LNG tank Over 70% of Americans oppose AI data centers; US protests intensify as more arrests are being made The Stop Data Center coalition claims that it isn’t against progress or that it wants to close down existing projects. Instead, it wants AI data center construction to be held until governments have established clearer rules on their development so that they do not have leave a negative impact on the environment and the people living around them. “AI, of course, is a super important ​technology and we ⁠need to have our own capacity,” EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen told the publication. But she also added that “it's very important for citizens that they can trust that their energy bills are not skyrocketing and there are not electricity blackouts because of ⁠data centers, ​or they are not destroying the environment with these projects.” Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors

items.titleZh: 抗议者冲击微软AI数据中心建设工地
items.descriptionZh:
据Tom's Hardware报道，荷兰阿姆斯特丹一座在建的微软数据中心被约百名抗议者涌入，部分抗议者举着“Screw your data center”（去你的数据中心）等标语。活动由“Stop Dirty Data Centers”联盟组织，计划于2026年11月6日至7日在16个国家同步采取行动，地点包括阿姆斯特丹、都柏林、华沙以及丹麦的另一处微软数据中心；该联盟网站地图显示，未来数日欧洲将有85个地点举行相关行动。数据中心所有者Pure Data Centers表示，尊重现场人员表达诉求，但“请现场人员安全离开，并就项目开发和关切与我们对话”。微软称理解公众的强烈情绪、尊重和平表达权利，但不纵容任何违法行为。

该联盟呼吁“立即暂停欧洲大型数据中心建设”，称AI数据中心在城镇和城市中“爆炸式扩张”，可能对人和地球的福祉造成“不可修复的伤害”。其列出的关切包括：本地社区受影响、就业与住房短缺、能源账单上涨、气候危机、热浪和水资源短缺、大型科技公司削弱民主、心理健康危机、监控增加与隐私侵蚀、安全化与军事化，以及有毒供应链。联盟表示，它并不反对进步，也不要求关闭现有项目，而是希望在各国政府建立更清晰的开发规则之前，暂缓新建AI数据中心，以免对环境和周边居民造成负面影响。

这一抗议反映出AI算力基础设施扩张正遭遇“社会许可”和监管阻力。数据中心是AI模型训练和推理的底层基础设施，通常具有高功率密度、高耗电、高冷却和水资源需求，并需要大规模电网接入和土地审批。争议核心并非反对AI技术本身，而是AI数据中心建设速度超过了能源、土地、环境与地方治理的承载能力。相关事件可能推高云与AI基础设施项目的延迟和合规成本，影响微软等公司的算力部署节奏，也会推动行业更重视旧工业区复用、高效冷却、可再生能源配套和社区协商。

类似阻力正在欧洲多地出现。芬兰方面，谷歌子公司Tuike Finland Oy被指无证毁坏816英亩森林，已遭刑事调查。丹麦因数据中心并网申请总量超过60GW——超过该国当前峰值用电量的8倍——已暂停受理相关并网请求。意大利一个地方议会则对农业用地上的数据中心开发设置200%税率，以鼓励开发商再利用旧工业区。欧盟科技主管Henna Virkkunen表示，AI是非常重要的技术，欧洲需要拥有自己的算力能力，但“对公民而言，非常重要的是他们能相信能源账单不会因数据中心而飙升，不会出现停电，也不会因这些项目破坏环境”。

在美国，数据中心反对已成为中期选举议题之一，文章称美国人以压倒性多数投票反对相关项目，表明阻力并不局限于美国。整体看，这篇新闻不涉及具体AI芯片架构或性能参数，而是聚焦AI数据中心扩张引发的能源、环境、隐私和地方治理冲突；其影响在于，AI基础设施的竞争不仅取决于芯片和资本，也取决于电网接入、环境审批、社区接受度和监管确定性。

items.title: Nvidia tightens tracking of AI GPUs in Southeast Asia as Chinese chip smuggling draws scrutiny, report claims
items.description: Nvidia is requiring Southeast Asian cloud providers seeking Nvidia Cloud Partner status to enroll in its Fleet Intelligence tracking program, giving the chipmaker greater visibility into where its AI GPUs are deployed. The move comes as Washington increases pressure over suspected chip smuggling into China, with investigations involving Megaspeed International and Super Micro highlighting the challenges of enforcing U.S. export restrictions
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Southeast Asia computing providers are now reportedly required to register with Nvidia's Fleet Intelligence tracking system if they want to become official Nvidia Cloud Partners (NCPs). The move, according to Bloomberg, is aimed at giving the chipmaker another way to monitor where its AI accelerators are deployed, as Washington grows increasingly frustrated with restricted hardware finding its way into China through regional smuggling networks. Nvidia was not immediately available for comment.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedThe NCP designation is worth pursuing as it gives cloud providers Nvidia's public endorsement and preferred access to its sought-after AI chips, putting the company in a position to use those benefits as leverage. Customers seeking the status must now enroll in Fleet Intelligence, according to people familiar with the new requirements. Fleet Management was introduced last December primarily as a data centre management tool. It gathers information about NVIDIA hardware deployed across participating companies' infrastructure, including the locations of individual accelerators. That information could give Nvidia a better picture of whether its chips are operating after they leave the supply chain.The system is, however, a universal tracking mandate. Participation has remained voluntary outside the NCP requirement, and Nvidia does not automatically receive location data from every customer using the software. The company has also not clarified whether existing Cloud Partners will have to enroll to retain their designation or whether the requirement will eventually extend beyond Southeast Asia.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Notably, Nvidia has been developing a way to locate AI for some time now. Last December, we reported that the company had developed software-based GPU tracking, using GPU telemetry and network latency measurements to estimate where processors are operating. Nvidia described the software as a customer-installed agent for monitoring hardware health, integrity and inventory.The technology has an obvious use beyond data maintenance. The U.S. restricts Chinese companies from purchasing advanced AI accelerators without a license, yet authorities believe billions of dollars worth of the hardware have reached Chinese buyers through third-party networks, with Southeast Asia becoming an important transit point for those transactions. You may like Investigative report details how export-restricted Nvidia AI chips reach China Nvidia tells data center operators to limit business from Chinese customers with new global restrictions, report claims Illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs found inside state-owned China Telecom's network A C4ADS investigation has previously identified several routes used to move restricted processors into China, including purchases through research initiatives, shell companies and shipments routed through other Southeast Asian countries. The nonprofit examined transactions between 2022 and 2025 and identified $13.4 million worth of Nvidia A100, H100, and AD102-series GPUs moving through regional trade routes. Its report also linked $4.6 billion in hardware purchases to Singapore-based Megaspeed International.Megaspeed has become a particularly awkward case for Nvidia, with the company being under U.S. and Singaporean investigation for more than a year over suspected chip diversion. Last week, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang defended his dealings with the firm, describing them as “completely normal,” adding, “we’ve studied all their deployments of our GPUs and counted every one.” Megaspeed denied any wrongdoing. In April, Megaspeed’s Malysisan data centre landlord terminated its contract, reallocating 68.4 megawatts of capacity to another cloud providerStay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsMoreover, Megaspeed is not the only example of how difficult it can be to police the movement of AI hardware. Earlier this year, U.S. prosecutors accused people associated with Super Micro of helping divert around $2.5 billion worth of Nvidia-powered servers to China through Southeast Asian intermediaries. The alleged scheme involved falsified paperwork and dummy server shells, with genuine hardware shipped onward after inspections. More recently, the company has faced additional scrutiny over its export compliance after inspections. Nvidia has also reportedly removed half of the Asian companies on its pre-approved buyer list and told cloud providers to keep at least 51% of their computing services with customers outside China. items.titleZh: 报道称，英伟达收紧对东南亚AI GPU的追踪，中国芯片走私引发审查
items.descriptionZh:
据报道，英伟达已要求东南亚地区的云计算服务商在申请成为官方“英伟达云合作伙伴”（NCP）时，必须注册其 Fleet Intelligence 追踪系统。彭博社称，此举旨在让英伟达多一种手段监控其 AI 加速器最终部署位置。当前美国政府对受限硬件通过区域走私网络流入中国日益不满，而东南亚被视为重要中转站。英伟达未立即置评。

NCP 资格具有实际商业价值：云服务商可获得英伟达的公开背书，并优先获得紧俏 AI 芯片供应，因此英伟达可将这些权益作为合规杠杆。知情人士称，申请 NCP 的客户现在必须加入 Fleet Intelligence。该系统对应的 Fleet Management 于去年 12 月推出，最初定位为数据中心管理工具，用于收集参与企业基础设施中英伟达硬件的部署信息，包括单个加速器的位置。这有助于英伟达判断芯片离开供应链后是否仍在预期地点运行。

技术层面，英伟达此前已开发基于软件的 GPU 追踪能力，利用 GPU 遥测数据和网络延迟测量来估算处理器运行位置。该软件被描述为由客户安装的代理程序，用于监控硬件健康、完整性和库存。其原理并非在芯片中植入硬件定位模块，而是通过客户侧软件采集运行与网络特征，推断设备所在区域。文章未披露定位精度、误差范围或支持的具体 GPU 型号等性能参数。该系统在 NCP 要求之外仍属自愿参与，英伟达也不会自动获得所有使用该软件客户的位置数据；现有 Cloud Partner 是否需要重新注册以保留资格、该要求是否会扩展到东南亚以外，均尚未明确。

这一机制的直接应用场景是出口管制合规与供应链追踪。美国限制中国企业未经许可购买先进 AI 加速器，但当局认为仍有数十亿美元硬件通过第三方网络进入中国，东南亚是重要通道。C4ADS 调查曾识别出通过研究项目、空壳公司和经其他东南亚国家转运等路线，并在 2022 至 2025 年交易中追踪到价值 1340 万美元的英伟达 A100、H100 和 AD102 系列 GPU 经区域贸易路线流动。该报告还将 46 亿美元硬件采购与总部位于新加坡的 Megaspeed International 联系起来。Megaspeed 因涉嫌芯片转移接受美国和新加坡调查已超过一年，英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋上周为其交易辩护称“完全正常”，并表示已研究其所有 GPU 部署、逐一清点；Megaspeed 否认不当行为。今年 4 月，Megaspeed 马来西亚数据中心房东终止合同，将 68.4 兆瓦容量转给另一家云服务商。

Megaspeed 并非孤例。今年早些时候，美国检方指控与 Super Micro 相关人员通过东南亚中间商，协助将约 25 亿美元英伟达服务器转运至中国，涉嫌使用伪造文件和空壳服务器，在检查后将真实硬件继续转运。此后该公司出口合规又受审查。英伟达据称已从其预批准买家名单中移除一半亚洲公司，并要求云服务商确保至少 51% 的计算服务面向中国以外客户。整体看，Fleet Intelligence 要求是英伟达将商业认证、芯片供应优先权与部署追踪绑定的一次合规创新，可能提升其对 AI 硬件流向的可见性，但也引发关于追踪范围、客户数据主权和是否向全球扩展的疑问。

items.title: Nvidia wants to repurpose over 130 old telco buildings as tiny data centers, report claims
items.description: Brightspeed has over 130 facilities located across the U.S., with Nvidia estimating that they could produce up to 1GW of compute capacity.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Internet and telecommunications provider Brightspeed is reportedly in talks with Nvidia to convert several of its buildings into tiny data centers. According to The Information, Nvidia pitched the idea to Apollo Global Management executives, the parent company of Brightspeed, who then asked it to submit written plans to the internet provider. Nvidia complied and has now requested additional information, data, and site visits to some of Brightspeed’s existing infrastructure.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleThe telecommunications company has around 130 buildings located around the country, many of which are already built to handle data and voice traffic and have the required power infrastructure to run Nvidia servers. Sources say that the AI tech giant estimates that these sites could collectively deliver around 1 gigawatt of compute capacity, which could accommodate more than 2,200 Supermicro Vera Rubin NVL72 racks containing 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs each. Although these sites already can power these GPUs, it’s still not a plug-and-play solution, as Nvidia would still need to install cooling systems and other supporting architecture. These would still require permits and approval from the local government, but they would likely face less red tape and opposition compared to building a data center from the ground up.Apollo Global Management has already made significant bets in AI hardware, with the asset management company involved in a $40 billion deal with SpaceX that would give it around 360,000 Vera Rubin GPUs across 5,000 NVL72 racks. While it’s currently unclear who will own the AI chips installed in Brightspeed facilities, the proposal could potentially help Apollo find a place for the Nvidia chips it ordered to get them up and running as soon as possible. This is a much better solution compared to waiting for years to get a data center approved, all while facing resistance from the community even after getting the go-ahead from the local government.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Having multiple small data centers like this is also a setup that OpenAI and Anthropic have been considering, especially as larger facilities are facing delays and backlash from the communities that they’re in. While having a large, homogeneous cluster built in one location is preferable for training, Nvidia representatives have described these smaller sites working together as an “inference network” to help run existing AI models. This is especially important as AI agents, which use five to ten times more tokens than humans, become more popular.The move to use existing facilities instead of building new ones from scratch has received renewed attention, especially after Americans overwhelmingly voted against data centers during the midterm elections. While the more than 300 data center bans enacted across the U.S. have only delayed three existing projects, it’s feared that the bans and moratoriums would make it that much harder to start new data center developments and make it difficult for AI companies to secure the compute capacity needed to power their AI models in the future. items.titleZh: 据报道，英伟达希望将130多栋旧电信建筑改造成小型数据中心
items.descriptionZh:
据The Information报道，美国互联网和电信提供商Brightspeed正与Nvidia洽谈，计划将旗下多栋建筑改造为小型数据中心。知情人士称，Nvidia向Brightspeed母公司Apollo Global Management的高管提出这一设想，后者要求Nvidia提交书面方案；Nvidia已照做，并进一步索取数据、补充信息，还要求实地考察Brightspeed部分现有基础设施。Brightspeed在全国约有130栋建筑，许多原本就用于承载数据和语音流量，具备运行Nvidia服务器所需的电力基础设施。Nvidia估计，这些站点合计可提供约1吉瓦算力，足以容纳超过2200个超微Vera Rubin NVL72机架；每个机架包含72颗Rubin GPU和36颗Vera CPU，按此计算约对应15.8万颗Rubin GPU和7.9万颗Vera CPU。不过，这并不是“即插即用”的方案：Nvidia仍需安装冷却系统和其他配套架构，并取得地方政府许可。相比从零新建数据中心，改造现有电信设施通常审批阻力更小、社区反对也可能更弱。

Apollo已在AI硬件领域大举下注。报道称，Apollo参与了一项与SpaceX相关的400亿美元交易，将获得约36万颗Vera Rubin GPU，分布在5000个NVL72机架中。目前尚不清楚Brightspeed设施内AI芯片的最终所有权，但该方案可能帮助Apollo为已订购的Nvidia芯片尽快找到部署地点，而不必等待多年审批和社区阻力。OpenAI和Anthropic也在考虑类似的多小型数据中心布局，因为大型吉瓦级项目面临延期和社区反弹。Nvidia代表将这种由多个小站点协同工作的模式称为“推理网络”，主要用于运行现有AI模型；训练任务仍更适合集中在单一地点的大规模同构集群。随着AI智能体普及——其token消耗量可达人类的5至10倍——分布式推理算力的重要性正在上升。这一趋势也与美国数据中心面临的政策环境有关：中期选举后，选民对数据中心反对情绪明显，全美已颁布300多项数据中心禁令，目前虽只延迟了3个现有项目，但业界担心禁令和暂停令将使新项目更难启动，并影响AI公司未来获取模型所需算力。

items.title: Tesla unveils AI accelerator roadmap, adopts new 'SI' branding in 'Super Intelligence' push
items.description: Tesla is ramping up its custom silicon ambitions with training-oriented Dojo D3 that can eventually go to orbital data centers and massive SI6 inference accelerator.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Tesla has disclosed its revamped AI accelerator roadmap that sheds some light on the future of the company's chip development efforts. The Elon Musk company expects that its 6th Generation inference accelerator will bring 80X more compute performance than the existing 4th Generation chip, whereas its D3 training accelerator will cease to use SRAM-centric architecture in favor of a multi-chiplet design with stacked HBM. Also, Tesla has adopted the term "super intelligence" instead of artificial intelligence for its AI accelerators, renaming them with SI monikers. Musk recently confirmed SpaceXAI would be redubbed SpaceXSI for the same reason.Wait a minute… I thought @elonmusk ’s Tesla chips were called AI4, AI5, and AI6. But in this latest presentation, they’re now labeled SI4, SI5, and SI6. Then I remembered: President Trump wants to replace “Artificial Intelligence” (AI) with “Super Intelligence” (SI). Looks like Elon Musk may already be embracing the new terminology. 🤔November 4, 2026 Swipe to scroll horizontally Row 0 - Cell 0 HW3 | AI3 SI4 | HW4 SI5 | AI5 SI6 | AI6 Dojo D1 Dojo D3 Application Inference Inference Inference Inference Training Training Process technology Samsung 14nm Samsung 7nm TSMC 3nm / Samsung 2nm 2nm-class TSMC 7nm TBD Architecture Monolithic Monolithic MCM MCM SoW Chiplets Packaging FCBGA FCBGA MCM MCM InFO_SoW (training tile) 2.5D + 3D Memory type LPDDR4 GDDR6 GDDR6/GDDR7 (?) GDDR7 (?) On-chip SRAM Stacked HBM Memory capacity 8 GB 16 GB 96 GB 144 GB 440 MB SRAM per die11 GB SRAM per wafer TBD Memory bandwidth ~68 GB/s ~224 GB/s TBD TBD ~10 TB/s (on-chip) TBD Performance vs. SI4 — 1X 40X 80X — — Estimated compute (TOPS) 72 TOPS 216 – 576 8,640 – 23,040 17,280 – 46,080 362 TFLOPS TBD Estimated compute (POPS) 0.072 0.216 – 0.576 8.64 – 23.04 17.28 – 46.08 0.362 PFLOPS TBD Status Legacy Production Nearing Production Development Discontinued Development Dojo D3: No more wafer-level integration?Perhaps the most interesting development in Tesla's AI hardware roadmap is the re-emergence of the in-house developed Dojo training accelerator after Elon Musk cancelled the whole wafer-level Dojo project in August, 2025, and then said SpaceX and xAI would exclusively use Nvidia hardware in August, 2026, both in its terrestrial and extraterrestrial data centers. Yet, the 3rd Generation Dojo will be considerably different from the first two generations, Dojo D1 and Dojo D2.Tesla describes its next-generation Dojo 3 (D3) training accelerator as a chiplet-based design that combines 2.5D and 3D packaging technologies with stacked HBM. This represents a substantial departure from the original Dojo D1 system-on-wafer architecture, which relied on distributed on-chip SRAM and interconnected 25 D1 processors with 11 GB of SRAM using wafer-scale packaging technology. The adoption of HBM suggests that Tesla intends to substantially increase memory capacity, as modern AI models consume extreme amounts of memory to store parameters, activations, and intermediate data, making SRAM unattractive from a capacity standpoint. The use of HBM simplifies memory scaling but introduces different latency, bandwidth, packaging, and power trade-offs. Yet, it remains unclear whether the company has abandoned wafer-scale integration altogether.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: On the one hand, it is possible to stack custom HBM modules on top of logic dies interconnected using wafer-scale packaging technology. On the other hand, wafer-level integration is expensive and makes the most sense for select use cases, which include SRAM-centric architectures. Stacking HBM atop wafer-scale interconnected logic dies adds further design complexities, cooling challenges, manufacturing complexity (i.e., potentially reducing yields), long-term reliability concerns, and ultimately costs. While most of the challenges can be resolved by adding redundancy and refining process technologies, this all comes at a cost, making wafer-scaling less likely for D3.Tesla has yet to disclose D3's compute performance, memory capacity, manufacturing process, or development schedule. At the same time, it claims that its Dojo D3 will be optimized for 'space, training, and scaling,' which means the unit will offer decent performance and will be easy to scale (which again points to a more conventional architecture of accelerators rather than to wafer-scale packaging). More intriguingly, the D3 is also set to be optimized for extraterrestrial deployments, which probably means radiation hardening for at least select SKUs. You may like ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC Huawei details AI accelerator roadmap, pulls in next-generation Ascend NPUs by several quarters Hot Chips 2026: Cerebras lays out the future of wafer-scale AI SI6: 80X more performance than HW4 in a few yearsAnother interesting detail in the roadmap is the disclosure of approximate compute performance of Tesla's 6th Generation inference accelerator (SI6): 80X compute improvement over HW4 and 9X more memory over HW4. Depending on how HW4 performance is measured (read on for explanation), we are talking about 17,280 – 46,080 TOPS (trillion operations per second), or 17.28 – 46.08 POPS (quadrillion operations per second), though we do not know anything about data formats supported by SI6. Of course, these are estimates, so take them with a grain of salt. To put the numbers into context, Nvidia's Rubin GPU offers 50 NVFP4 PFLOPS for inference, 35 NVFP4 PFLOPS for training, and 17.5 FP8/FP6 PFLOPS. Meanwhile, Rubin is shipping to customers today, whereas SI6 is due in 2029 – 2030. There are some additional details about SI6, which we will discuss below.Tesla's existing 4th Generation inference processor used in the company's automobiles today (which was originally called HW4, then renamed to AI4, then to SI4) is made by Samsung Foundry using its 7nm-class process technology and relies on conventional flip-chip ball grid array (FCBGA) packaging (note that the alleged Tesla slide contains a mistake and claims that the unit is made using a 5nm-class node) as well as presumably 16 GB of GDDR6 memory. The company describes the processor as the current benchmark for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology, which makes it the baseline against which performance of future generations is measured. Meanwhile, Tesla does not officially disclose the chip's absolute compute performance numbers, memory capacity, or power consumption, which makes comparison hard. Elon Musk once said that HW4 is 3X – 8X more powerful than HW3, which was officially rated at 72 TOPS, making HW4 a 216 – 576 TOPS ASIC (note that these are estimates).Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsAs expected, the slide re-confirms that the upcoming 5th Generation inference accelerator called SI5 (aka HW5 aka AI5) will be manufactured using 3nm- and 2nm-class process technologies at TSMC and Samsung Foundry, respectively, and will adopt a multi-chip module (MCM) design, marking a departure from the conventional packaging approach used for HW4. Tesla expects SI5 to deliver a 40X performance improvement over HW4, which will be a result of an eightfold increase in compute capabilities (driven by considerably denser process technologies and more execution units) and a fivefold gain from silicon optimization, according to Elon Musk, which points to 8,640 – 23,040 TOPS (an estimated figure), depending on how one counts performance of HW4. Meanwhile, the processor is expected to consume from 250W to 800W depending on application, so making performance estimates at this point is not exactly a good business. Meanwhile, the processor will also feature six times more memory than its predecessor (i.e., 96 GB). Depending on the memory type used (GDDR6 or GDDR7), the Tesla SI5 can offer memory bandwidth between 768 GB/s and 1.536 GB/s.Moving on to the Tesla's 6th Generation inference accelerator (SI6), which is set to further increase compute performance to 80 times that of HW4 and feature eight times more memory than the current-generation processor. This could translate to 17.28 – 46.08 POPS (quadrillion operations per second), depending on how to count HW4 performance, and 144 GB of memory, which is significant performance and amount of memory for an AI accelerator.Tesla has already inked a deal with Samsung Foundry to make its 6th Generation inference accelerators through 2033, and the new slide reveals that the unit will be made using a 2nm-class process technology. Given the fact that the chip is due in 2029 – 2030 and Samsung's recently updated foundry roadmap, we are probably talking about automotive-grade SF2A, performance-enhanced SF2P, or even SF2Z with backside power delivery. Meanwhile, a thing that strikes the eye with the SI6 is that Tesla does not envision the chip to be produced at Terafab using Intel's 14A fabrication process in the 2030s.SI6 will retain the multi-chip module (MCM) approach introduced with AI5/SI5/HW5, which seems rational as it will be able to leverage experience it is going to get with its 5th Generation inference accelerator and retain relatively reasonable packaging costs. Many automakers are considering adoption of multi-chiplet designs and HBM memory for their next-generation system-in-packages (SiPs), which will drive their costs. It remains to be seen when Tesla adopts HBM for its inference accelerators, but probably not with SI6. items.titleZh: 特斯拉发布AI加速器路线图，采用全新“SI”品牌推进“超级智能”布局
items.descriptionZh:
特斯拉近日公布更新后的AI加速器路线图，较系统地披露了从当前车载推理芯片到未来训练芯片的演进方向。公司将AI加速器统一改称“SI”（Super Intelligence），产品线包括已量产的SI4（即HW4/AI4）、接近量产的SI5（HW5/AI5）、开发中的SI6（AI6），以及训练芯片Dojo D1和D3。马斯克还确认SpaceXAI将更名为SpaceXSI。报道提到，这一命名变化更多是品牌和话术调整，并不改变芯片架构标准；但其路线图显示，特斯拉正从单体芯片逐步转向多芯片模块（MCM）、chiplet和HBM，应用范围也从车载推理扩展到训练甚至太空部署。

当前SI4/HW4采用三星7nm级工艺（新闻称幻灯片误写为5nm级）、FCBGA封装和约16GB GDDR6内存，内存带宽约224GB/s，是特斯拉FSD的当前性能基准。特斯拉未官方公布其绝对算力、功耗等数据；若按HW3官方72TOPS、马斯克称HW4为HW3的3至8倍推算，SI4大约为216至576TOPS。下一代SI5计划由台积电3nm级和三星2nm级工艺制造，采用MCM多芯片模块设计，内存提升至约96GB，可能使用GDDR6或GDDR7，带宽约768GB/s至1.536GB/s（原文如此，疑为TB/s笔误），功耗预计250W至800W。特斯拉称SI5相对HW4有40倍性能提升，其中约8倍来自计算能力提升、5倍来自硅片优化，推算约8,640至23,040TOPS。

SI6的目标更激进：相对HW4提升80倍算力，内存约144GB，约为SI4的9倍（文中另一处又称8倍）。按前述HW4估算口径，SI6算力约17,280至46,080TOPS，即17.28至46.08POPS。它将采用2nm级工艺和MCM设计，预计2029至2030年推出，三星已签约代工至2033年，可能使用汽车级SF2A、增强型SF2P甚至带背面供电的SF2Z工艺；报道还指出，SI6并未规划在2030年代由英特尔14A工艺的Terafab生产。作为参照，英伟达Rubin GPU已提供50 NVFP4 PFLOPS推理、35 NVFP4 PFLOPS训练和17.5 FP8/FP6 PFLOPS，且已开始交付，而SI6要晚数年，因此这些TOPS数字只能视为特斯拉的估算目标，且其支持的数据格式尚未披露，跨架构直接比较需谨慎。

训练芯片方面，Dojo D3在特斯拉2025年8月取消晶圆级Dojo项目、2026年8月又称SpaceX和xAI将主要使用英伟达硬件之后重新出现在路线图中。D3将放弃D1以SRAM为中心的晶圆级系统（SoW）架构，改为chiplet设计，结合2.5D和3D封装并堆叠HBM。D1曾采用台积电7nm、晶圆级封装，将25个D1处理器与11GB SRAM互连，单die片上SRAM为440MB，片上带宽约10TB/s，算力约362TFLOPS。D3改用HBM可显著提升内存容量，更适合大模型训练中参数、激活值和中间数据的存储需求，但也会带来延迟、带宽、封装、散热和功耗方面的新权衡。特斯拉尚未公布D3的算力、内存容量、制程和进度，只称其针对“太空、训练和扩展”优化，并可能为外星部署做抗辐射加固。由于晶圆级封装叠加HBM在成本、良率、冷却和可靠性上挑战很大，D3更可能采用较常规的chiplet加速器架构，而非继续晶圆级集成。

总体看，特斯拉自研芯片的核心影响在于：通过SI系列和Dojo D3降低对英伟达等外部AI硬件的依赖，为FSD、自动驾驶训练和未来数据中心/太空计算场景提供定制化算力。SI5和SI6若达到目标，将显著提升车载推理和数据中心训练能力，MCM与HBM方向也符合行业趋势；但其时间表较晚、成本与汽车级可靠性挑战突出，且英伟达等竞争对手迭代更快，实际竞争力仍待产品落地验证。

items.title: Protesters break into Microsoft data center site in Amsterdam
items.description:
Members of the action group Geef Tegengas put a banner on a crane during a protest. | Image: Getty Images	

Protesters have broken into a construction site of a new Microsoft data center in Amsterdam this morning. Members of the Geef Tegengas group helped organize the protest against the construction of three 85-meter data center towers in the outskirts of Amsterdam.
