Read the full story at The Verge.
items.content: Protesters have broken into a construction site of a new Microsoft data center in Amsterdam this morning. Members of the Geef Tegengas group helped organize the protest against the construction of three 85-meter data center towers in the outskirts of Amsterdam.Reuters reports that around 100 people made it into the construction site, with some scaling a crane to place a “fuck AI” banner. Protesters also unfurled a “Microsoft powers genocide” banner on the construction site, and chanted “Microsoft has got to go” and “free Palestine.”Opposition to the new data center in Amsterdam comes more than a year after the city banned new data centers until 2030, after a temporary stop that was announced at the end of 2023. Microsoft will be the sole tenant of this new data center, and the project is proceeding as it was planned as far back as 2016, before a ban was put in place. The site, being built by British developer Pure Data Centres, has also managed to navigate some loopholes to reach the construction stage.RelatedMicrosoft employee disrupts 50th anniversary and calls AI boss ‘war profiteer’Microsoft employees occupy headquarters in protest of Israel contractsMicrosoft employee disrupts Satya Nadella’s keynote with ‘Free Palestine’ protestMicrosoft blocks the Israeli military from some cloud and AI servicesThe protests over Microsoft’s data center site in Amsterdam comes in the same week that activists staged a mock Israeli military checkpoint outside a Microsoft data center in Dublin on Tuesday, part of a wave of data center protests across Europe. Earlier this week, voters across the US also rejected unrestrained development of data centers. AI data centers are continuing to pop up across the US, with frequent opposition from locals concerned about the impact on their communities.Microsoft also abandoned the UK’s largest data center project last month, after local electricity grid officials said the site won’t be supplied with power until the 2030s. The software maker has also faced a wave of protests from former employees over the past year. Microsoft’s 50th anniversary party was interrupted by employees protesting the use of Microsoft’s technologies in Israel’s war against Hamas, with one calling Microsoft’s AI CEO, Mustafa Suleyman, a “war profiteer.“A Microsoft employee also disrupted the company’s Build developer conference last year, interrupting Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella’s keynote. Months later, Microsoft fired two employee protesters who occupied its president’s office.

items.titleZh: 抗议者闯入阿姆斯特丹微软数据中心工地
items.descriptionZh:
今早，约100名抗议者闯入微软位于荷兰阿姆斯特丹的一处新数据中心施工现场，反对在阿姆斯特丹郊区建设三座85米高的数据中心塔。抗议由Geef Tegengas等团体协助组织。据路透社报道，部分抗议者爬上起重机悬挂“fuck AI”横幅，并在工地展开“Microsoft powers genocide”横幅，高喊“Microsoft has got to go”和“free Palestine”等口号。事件将AI数据中心扩张、能源与土地占用、社区反对以及微软与以色列相关合同争议交织在一起。

背景方面，阿姆斯特丹在2023年底宣布临时停止后，已禁止在2030年前新建数据中心；但微软该项目的规划可追溯至2016年，早于禁令出台。微软将是该数据中心的唯一租户，项目由英国开发商Pure Data Centres建设，并通过一些漏洞推进至施工阶段。报道没有披露该数据中心的具体AI算力、芯片架构、冷却方案或能效参数，因此无法从原文获得技术原理和性能对比数据；从新闻语境看，该项目属于承载微软云与AI服务的大型数据中心基础设施，其规模以三座85米塔为标志，核心争议更多集中在选址、能源供应和伦理政治层面。

这一抗议并非孤立事件。同一周，活动人士在都柏林微软数据中心外设置模拟以色列军事检查站，构成欧洲数据中心抗议潮的一部分；本周美国选民也否决了不受限制的数据中心开发，美国各地AI数据中心持续涌现并频繁遭遇当地居民反对。微软上月还放弃了英国最大数据中心项目，原因是当地电网官员表示该站点要到2030年代才能获得供电。过去一年，微软还面临前员工抗议：公司50周年活动被员工打断，抗议微软技术被用于以色列对哈马斯的战争，有人称微软AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman为“war profiteer”；一名员工还打断了Build开发者大会上CEO Satya Nadella的主题演讲，数月后微软解雇了两名占领总裁办公室的抗议员工。

技术影响和应用场景上，AI数据中心是云计算和大模型训练推理的关键基础设施，但需要大量电力、土地和水资源，选址与供电瓶颈正成为项目落地的主要约束。阿姆斯特丹案例显示，即使城市层面设置新建禁令，早期规划项目和开发漏洞仍可能让大型数据中心推进，进而激化社区、气候与政治伦理争议。对美国与欧洲而言，AI数据中心扩张将越来越依赖电网扩容、能效提升和更透明的选址治理；对企业而言，微软等云与AI服务商需要在基础设施扩张、地方许可、能源供给和员工/公众伦理诉求之间取得平衡。

items.title: Gelsinger-backed Nagare Labs’ Z2RAM promises SRAM speed at DRAM density
items.description: Georgia Tech spinout Nagare Labs, backed by Playground Global, unveils Z2RAM, a capacitorless memory to stack on AI accelerators.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A Pat Gelsinger-backed Georgia Tech spinout, Nagare Labs, says its Z2RAM can put SRAM-speed memory, at DRAM density, directly on top of AI chips. The founders’ own papers show a fast-improving cell that, tested up to 85 degrees Celsius, holds data for over 300 seconds. Gen 1 is projected to have 5x SRAM density with six stacked layers, 14x DRAM speed, and 3x less read energy than SRAM.AI chips require a lot of bandwidth, and it has been challenging to get sufficient yields of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to feed them. Even when manufacturers can get it, some reportedly plan to settle for fewer layers for yield reasons, and heat is another. Heat is also why Samsung’s zHBM, which stacks DRAM directly on the processor, is planned at only about four layers.Alternatives include high-bandwidth flash, still in development, which stacks NAND like HBM and would sit beside the GPU, or SRAM stacked directly on the die, which is less dense and more expensive for the capacity, but also faster. DRAM, which is more capacious, can sit on top of the compute, but heat limits how hard the logic underneath can run.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: That limit is already shaping chipmakers’ design path for stacked memory. Micron’s vHBM plans, for example, include heat-spreading structures. With HBM stacked on a logic die, and DRAM needing to be kept at or below 95 degrees Celsius, the logic’s heat output is capped at 220 W/cm², or 300 W/cm² with better thermal vias, according to a 2025 simulation by co-founder Shimeng Yu’s group. Nagare Labs says peak compute has grown 70% a year over the past three decades, against 20% for memory bandwidth. (Image credit: J. Sharda et al., IEEE JxCDC (CC BY 4.0), cropped)The company describes its Z2RAM as “Two transistors and a shield. No capacitor,” where a write transistor places a charge on a storage node and the shield blocks noisy neighbors. The read transistor can sense without draining. In a gain cell like this, the read transistor’s gate capacitance holds the charge, so reads are non-destructive and the cell avoids DRAM’s write-back. Nagare aims for well under a picojoule per bit. You may like Hot Chips 2026: d-Matrix stacks AI accelerator directly on custom DRAM for 100 TB/s per card Micron details ambitious DRAM and NAND roadmap — 3D NAND, High-NA EUV, new materials, and custom silicon makes a comeback Micron's next-generation 3D NAND to double bit density with over 400 layers, offering extreme performance Nagare builds Z2RAM by depositing its layers on top of the accelerator and patterning them “together on one die,” much as 3D NAND flash scales by adding layers. There’s no interposer and no bonds between the memory layers, which is part of the secret sauce. One lithography exposure covers several layers at once, and standard 300 mm tools with DUV do the job, with no EUV required. The current roadmap is aiming at over 100 layers with “hundreds of thousands” of vertical connections.Retaining data at higher temperatures is the challenge, and one the founders have probed repeatedly with their testing. A 2020 paper from co-founder Suman Datta’s group, on a tungsten-doped indium oxide two-transistor cell, had retention of 1 second at 25 degrees Celsius and just 300 milliseconds at 85°C. An update in 2025, which has Datta as a co-author, adds a third transistor and removes the gate overlap from its transistors, managing over 1,000 seconds at 25°C, up from 200 seconds with overlapped ones. It also simulated a GPU L2 at twice SRAM’s capacity but in the same area with 75–80% lower energy-delay-area product, a combined score that multiplies energy, delay and area.Six months later, both founders showed a “folded asymmetric boosted” three-transistor cell that held data for over 300 seconds at 85°C, as compared to only 100 milliseconds for a conventional three-transistor design. That’s still below the roughly 95°C that Nagare says DRAM must stay under, so neither the founders’ published cells nor Z2RAM have shown retention above that line yet. The boosted cell is also “refresh-free,” which means data in the GPU’s last-level cache, profiled from AI workloads, doesn’t have time to decay before it is overwritten. Swipe to scroll horizontally What the founders’ papers measured and simulated, and what Nagare projects Figure Value Measured, simulated or projected Conditions Source 2020 two-transistor cell, retention 1 s; 300 ms Measured 25°C; 85°C Datta’s group, IEDM 2020 2025 three-transistor cell (self-aligned), retention More than 1,000 s Measured 25°C Georgia Tech, IEDM 2025 Conventional three-transistor cell, retention 0.1 s Measured 85°C, to a 100 mV decay Georgia Tech, VLSI 2026 Boosted three-transistor cell, retention More than 300 s Measured 85°C, to a 100 mV decay Georgia Tech, VLSI 2026 Write pulse 10 ns Measured Two-transistor cell Georgia Tech, IEDM 2025 Read delay 2.6 ns Simulated 7nm design, 128×128 array Georgia Tech, VLSI 2026 Cell area 0.0168 µm² Projected 7nm design rules Georgia Tech, VLSI 2026 Bit density 5.7× that of 7nm SRAM Simulated Four tiers, 256MB, same area Yu’s group, IEEE Trans. Computers 2026 GPU L2 energy-delay-area product 75–80% lower than SRAM Simulated Twice the capacity in the same area Georgia Tech, IEDM 2025 Logic power under stacked DRAM 220 W/cm² (300 W/cm² with better thermal vias) Simulated DRAM kept at 95°C or below Yu’s group, JxCDC 2025 Nagare Gen 1 density 5× SRAM Projected Six layers, vs. 2nm HD SRAM Nagare Labs Nagare Gen 1 speed 14× faster than DRAM Projected Gen 1 Nagare Labs Nagare Gen 1 read energy 3× less than SRAM Projected Gen 1 Nagare Labs Physical space is also limited for this application, and the founders project their boosted cell at 0.0168 µm² at 7nm, compared with 0.0199 µm² for a high-density SRAM cell on TSMC’s 3nm (N3) process. A separate study from Yu’s group found that a four-tier, 256MB cache of two-transistor gain cells at 7nm could reach 5.7x the bit density of 7nm SRAM in the same area, in simulation. However, the return on investment falls off past seven or eight tiers because masks scale with layers. Nagare Labs’ claim of single lithography would potentially bypass this limitation.That has not yet been proven, and nothing published yet shows it. “Where we are is literally lab prototypes,” Datta told The Register, adding that sampling of Z2RAM tiles is targeted within four years and production shipments, if they arrive, within the next decade. Yu told the outlet that no standard yet exists for integrating this kind of memory with an accelerator, which means Nagare might have to come up with the interface itself. Datta also mentioned reliability to the outlet, as single-electron effects can shift a cell’s threshold enough to upset the stored bit. It also remains to be seen if the tested three-transistor cells work sufficiently well as a two-transistor, single-shield product. What to read next CXMT president says company’s first 4F² DRAM will be a server DDR5 RDIMM due by year-end Hot Chips 2026: High Bandwidth Flash promises massive bandwidth and capacity, but its usability is extremely limited Micron plans to use wafer bonding and High-NA EUV for next-gen DRAM Even if Nagare clears those hurdles, a more important one lingers: It currently has no fab. The plan to scale depends on getting partners for fabrication as well as packaging. Nagare is reportedly looking for an R&D fab partner so it can scale beyond the university clean room. Perhaps the most similar type of memory-on-compute shipping today, and the one Datta cited to the outlet as a model for working with chipmakers, is AMD’s 3D V-Cache.Z2RAM isn’t the first capacitorless memory to promise a 5x improvement over SRAM in density; it follows in the footsteps of Innovative Silicon’s Z-RAM from 20 years ago, a technology AMD licensed, though it was not pursued. A Georgia Tech paper due at IEDM in December covers a different device, a one-transistor, one-ferroelectric-transistor cell, aimed at the same gap between SRAM latency and DRAM density.Gelsinger, previously CEO of Intel, which started as a memory company, phased out Optane, a low-latency non-volatile memory, in favor of CXL. Optane sought to bridge the gap between slower non-volatile storage, such as HDDs and standard SSDs, and DRAM. Now he sits on Nagare’s board, and Playground Global, where he is a general partner, led the startup’s $5 million round as Nagare searches for a solution to a different but related problem.Nagare declined to share measured retention, latency, or energy figures. The founders’ boosted cell already holds data at 85°C longer than a cache needs, but until a fab-built, multi-layer Z2RAM stack is measured, retention above 95°C included, its headline numbers remain projections.

items.titleZh: 获基辛格支持的 Nagare Labs 旗下 Z2RAM 承诺以 DRAM 密度实现 SRAM 速度
items.descriptionZh:
由前英特尔CEO帕特·基辛格支持的佐治亚理工学院衍生公司Nagare Labs声称，其Z2RAM技术能够将SRAM速度的内存以DRAM的密度直接堆叠在AI芯片上方。创始人自己发表的论文显示，这种存储单元性能正在快速提升，在高达85摄氏度的测试温度下可将数据保持超过300秒。据预测，第一代产品将实现5倍于SRAM的密度（采用六层堆叠）、14倍于DRAM的速度，以及比SRAM低3倍的读取能耗。

AI芯片需要大量带宽，而获得足够良率的高带宽内存（HBM）来为其供料一直颇具挑战。即便制造商能够实现，据报道一些厂商出于良率考虑计划接受较少的堆叠层数，散热则是另一个问题。散热也是三星zHBM计划仅采用约四层堆叠的原因——该技术将DRAM直接堆叠在处理器上。替代方案包括仍在开发中的高带宽闪存，它将NAND像HBM一样堆叠并置于GPU旁边；或者将SRAM直接堆叠在裸片上，后者密度较低、单位容量成本更高，但速度更快。容量更大的DRAM可以置于计算单元上方，但散热限制了下方逻辑电路能跑多高的频率。这一限制已经在塑造芯片制造商对堆叠内存的设计路径。例如，美光的vHBM计划包含散热结构。根据联合创始人Shimeng Yu团队2025年的一项仿真研究，当HBM堆叠在逻辑裸片上、且DRAM需要保持在95摄氏度或以下时，逻辑电路的发热量被限制在220 W/cm²，若采用更好的散热通孔则可达到300 W/cm²。Nagare Labs表示，过去三十年间峰值算力每年增长70%，而内存带宽每年仅增长20%。

该公司将其Z2RAM描述为“两个晶体管加一个屏蔽层，无需电容器”——写晶体管将电荷放置在存储节点上，屏蔽层则隔绝相邻单元的噪声干扰，读晶体管可以在不消耗电荷的情况下感测数据。在这种增益单元中，读晶体管的栅极电容保持电荷，因此读取是非破坏性的，单元无需像DRAM那样进行写回操作。Nagare的目标是每比特能耗远低于1皮焦耳。

Nagare通过将各层沉积在加速器上方并在“同一裸片上一起”图案化来构建Z2RAM，这与3D NAND闪存通过增加层数来扩展的方式非常相似。内存层之间没有中介层、没有键合，这是其核心秘诀之一。一次光刻曝光可同时覆盖多个层，使用标准300毫米DUV工具即可完成，无需EUV。当前路线图的目标是超过100层，并实现“数十万”个垂直连接。

在更高温度下保持数据是核心挑战，创始人已通过反复测试对此进行了探索。2020年联合创始人Suman Datta团队发表的一篇论文，针对钨掺杂氧化铟双晶体管单元，在25摄氏度下保持时间为1秒，而在85摄氏度下仅为300毫秒。2025年的更新版本（Datta为合著者）增加了第三个晶体管并消除了晶体管的栅极重叠，在25摄氏度下实现了超过1000秒的保持时间，而重叠版本为200秒。该研究还模拟了一个容量为SRAM两倍但面积相同的GPU L2缓存，其能量-延迟-面积乘积（一个综合能耗、延迟和面积的评分指标）降低了75%至80%。六个月后，两位创始人展示了一种“折叠非对称升压”三晶体管单元，在85摄氏度下可将数据保持超过300秒，而传统三晶体管设计仅为100毫秒。这仍低于Nagare所说的DRAM必须保持在约95摄氏度以下的要求，因此创始人已发表的单元和Z2RAM都尚未展示出在该温度线以上的保持能力。该升压单元还是“免刷新”的，这意味着GPU最后一级缓存中来自AI工作负载的数据在被覆盖之前不会随时间衰减。

物理空间对该应用也构成限制。创始人在7纳米工艺下将其升压单元的面积投影为0.0168 µm²，而台积电3纳米（N3）工艺的高密度SRAM单元为0.0199 µm²。Yu团队的另一项研究发现，在仿真中，7纳米工艺下四层256MB的双晶体管增益单元缓存在相同面积下可达到7纳米SRAM位密度的5.7倍。然而，超过七八层后投资回报率会下降，因为掩膜成本随层数增加而增加。Nagare Labs声称的单次光刻技术可能绕过这一限制，但这尚未得到验证，目前也没有任何已发表成果证明这一点。

“我们目前所处的阶段就是实验室原型，”Datta对《The Register》表示，并补充说Z2RAM芯片样品的送样目标是在四年内实现，量产出货（如果能实现的话）则在未来十年内。Yu对该媒体表示，目前尚无将此类内存与加速器集成的标准，这意味着Nagare可能不得不自行开发接口。Datta还向该媒体提到了可靠性问题，因为单电子效应可能使单元的阈值偏移到足以破坏存储比特的程度。此外，已测试的三晶体管单元能否作为双晶体管单屏蔽产品足够良好地工作，仍有待观察。

即便Nagare克服了这些障碍，一个更重要的障碍依然存在：该公司目前没有晶圆厂。其扩展计划取决于能否获得制造和封装方面的合作伙伴。据报道，Nagare正在寻找研发晶圆厂合作伙伴，以便将规模扩展到大学洁净室之外。目前最接近量产的存算一体内存类型——也是Datta向该媒体提及作为与芯片制造商合作范本的——是AMD的3D V-Cache。

Z2RAM并非首个承诺密度比SRAM提升5倍的无电容内存；它追随的是20年前Innovative Silicon公司的Z-RAM技术的脚步，AMD曾授权该技术但并未继续推进。佐治亚理工学院一篇计划于12月在IEDM发表的论文涉及另一种器件——单晶体管单铁电晶体管单元，瞄准的是SRAM延迟与DRAM密度之间的同一空白。

基辛格曾任英特尔CEO，而英特尔最初是一家内存公司，后来放弃了低延迟非易失性内存Optane，转而押注CXL。Optane旨在弥合较慢的非易失性存储（如HDD和标准SSD）与DRAM之间的差距。如今基辛格担任Nagare董事会成员，他所在的General Partner公司Playground Global领投了这家初创企业500万美元的融资，而Nagare正在寻找一个不同但相关问题的解决方案。Nagare拒绝分享实测的保持时间、延迟或能耗数据。创始人已发表的升压单元在85摄氏度下保持数据的时间已超过缓存所需，但在晶圆厂制造的多层Z2RAM堆叠被实测（包括95摄氏度以上的保持能力）之前，其 headline 数据仍只是预测。

items.titleZh: OpenAI不再要求数据中心项目签署保密协议
items.descriptionZh:
在美国中期选举中选民强烈反对数据中心扩张的背景下，OpenAI宣布对其数据中心项目所在社区作出一系列新承诺，其中最受关注的是不再与公职人员签署保密协议（NDA）。此前，许多数据中心项目因依赖NDA隐藏开发商与地方官员之间的讨论而受到审查。OpenAI表示，今后与公共官员的协议仅保留“窄范围保护”，覆盖合法的安全信息、商业秘密以及专有或具有竞争敏感性的信息。这一做法与亚马逊10月的表态形成呼应：亚马逊当时宣布，不再在与政府机构合作的数据中心项目中使用NDA。相关报道亦指出，数据中心议题在中期选举中遭遇挫折。

除NDA承诺外，OpenAI还承诺支付其数据中心“全部用电成本”以及“为服务我们所需的基础设施”成本。公司将通过公布预计创造的岗位和报告招聘情况，为当地社区提供机会。OpenAI称，未来由该公司拥有并运营的每一个“计算园区”（其对数据中心的新称呼）都将制定一份“本地契约”，纳入上述承诺，并反映“当地优先事项”。

从技术与社会许可角度看，数据中心属于高耗电、强基础设施依赖型设施，其扩张不仅涉及算力部署，也涉及电网容量、能源成本和地方公共资源。OpenAI的新承诺实质上试图将电力与配套基础设施成本内部化，并通过就业透明和本地契约机制回应社区对成本转嫁、信息不透明和利益分配不均的担忧。原文未披露具体性能参数或算力指标，因此可对比的数据主要是政策层面：OpenAI与亚马逊均开始放弃对政府机构的广泛NDA，转而采用有限保密保护；OpenAI还进一步将电力成本、基础设施成本和本地就业报告纳入社区承诺。若这些承诺落地，可能推动数据中心行业提高选址与审批透明度，改善开发商与地方政府、居民之间的信任关系，并为未来算力基础设施扩张建立新的社区沟通范式。

随后节目转向AI商业化难题：是否有人真正找到在AI上赚钱的方法？OpenAI在网页搜索上的快速增长是否具有商业意义，尤其是在谷歌也尚未解决AI网页搜索盈利问题的情况下。节目提到企业正在缩减相关投入，AI代理并未如预期接管业务；AI领域资金流动规模很大，但流入是否足以支撑整个生态持续运转仍是关键问题。

节目最后还涵盖“Brendan Carr Is a Dummy”环节、SpaceX的移动业务野心、触摸屏MacBook、RAM Altman等话题，并回顾云游戏挑战、数据中心选举、Rian Johnson的新iPhone应用以及阅读的未来。整体而言，这是一期以政策、商业和行业趋势为主的播客导览，并未展开具体芯片技术原理或性能参数对比。

history.content: inMusic, the parent company of Akai, Moog, Native Instruments, and more, has decided to embrace the modding community. In an interview with The Verge, inMusic CEO Jack O’Donnell said, “We’re going to provide a toolbox to the community, we’re going to provide the inner workings of, say, an MPC or Sample so that people can do what they want.” That “toolbox” includes making the code for devices like the recently teased MPC Sample Key open source, but also offering developers an SDK to make modifications easier and lessen the risk of bricking your beloved sampler.While Akai is eager to see what the modding community cooks up, and has started seeding devices to developers ahead of the official release of the Sample Key, the company takes reliability seriously. O’Donnell said the company wants to “make sure that our official software is completely stable and good for an artist on stage.” He can’t have Fred Again going on stage and discovering his MPC is riddled with bugs. But he also wants people to feel comfortable tinkering. “We’ll try to give them a reset button,” he said so “They can experiment with it, and then not lose what they have.”The company is planning to make a big splash NAMM, the annual convention of music manufacturers in Anaheim, with Creator Lab, where it will let technically curious musicians get some hands-on time hacking 22 new products from across its brands. That includes products from Moog, that might not seem like a natural pairing for vibe coding because of its analog design. But O’Donnell thinks it can be, “if we open it up correctly.” That will involve building a platform for devs to work around the analog parts of the circuit.Other companies have also embraced the modding community. Erica Synths recently released the source code for its LXR-02 drum machine, Polyend open-sourced its line of Tracker grooveboxes, and Behringer has also announced a slew of open-source devices, including a $150 clone of the MPC One called Kick, a clone of the E-mu SP-1200, the Anima DJ controller, the Ignite sequencer, and the Polykeys 61 MIDI controller.The change in the industry has been quick and seismic. O’Donnell said of the need to provide developers tools for hacking inMusic’s products, “I can tell you it wasn’t on our task list five weeks ago. It just all of a sudden has to be on a task list now.”Of course, not everyone is thrilled. Elektron has expressed mixed feelings about the emergence of vibe-coded mods. The company banned linking to hacks and modified firmware from its official forums, though not discussing them generally, citing concerns about the possibility of damaging instruments. A statement posted on its forums says: “We would always warn against modifications to our firmware and/or machines that could brick them (potentially rendering them unusable), prevent future updates, affect warranty coverage.”While Elektron doesn’t want people posting links to hacked Digitone firmware on its forums, it’s not actively trying to thwart the modding community. The consensus is there’s no going back now that vibe coding has upended the music gear world, and trying to stand in the way would be a mistake. inMusic’s O’Donnell told the Verge, “you can try to wall them off, which is just a losing battle one … and so we want to embrace them.”
history.author: Terrence O’Brien
history.titleZh: How Akai and Moog are embracing vibe-coded mods
history.descriptionZh:
inMusic——Akai、Moog、Native Instruments等音乐设备品牌的母公司——正在转向拥抱硬件改装与开源社区。该公司CEO Jack O’Donnell在接受The Verge采访时表示，inMusic计划向社区提供“工具箱”，开放MPC、Sample等设备的内部运作信息，让用户按自己的需求进行修改。具体措施包括将近期预告的MPC Sample Key等设备的代码开源，并向开发者提供SDK，以降低改装门槛和设备“变砖”的风险。Akai一方面希望看到改装社区做出新东西，并已在Sample Key正式发布前向开发者发放设备；另一方面仍强调可靠性，称必须确保官方软件对舞台艺人完全稳定，不能让艺人在演出时遇到满身bug的MPC。为此，公司计划提供“重置按钮”式恢复机制，让用户放心实验而不丢失原有内容。

在技术路径上，inMusic的创新不在于单一性能参数，而在于把原本封闭的音乐硬件固件、应用层和开发接口部分开放给社区，并通过SDK和恢复机制在“可改装”与“可演出”之间建立平衡。公司还计划在阿纳海姆举行的NAMM展会期间推出Creator Lab，让对技术感兴趣的音乐人亲手hack其跨品牌22款新品，其中包括Moog产品。Moog以模拟电路设计著称，看似不适合社区快速实验性改装，但O’Donnell认为只要开放方式正确仍可行，并将围绕模拟电路部分为开发者构建平台。新闻未披露这些产品的具体处理器、延迟、复音数等性能指标，重点在于生态策略：用官方稳定版本服务现场演出，用开放工具服务开发者和DIY用户。

行业层面，音乐硬件开放源码和改装正在快速升温。Erica Synths已发布LXR-02鼓机源码，Polyend开源了Tracker系列groovebox，Behringer也宣布多款开源设备，包括售价150美元的MPC One克隆Kick、E-mu SP-1200克隆、Anima DJ控制器、Ignite音序器和Polykeys 61 MIDI控制器。O’Donnell称，为开发者提供改装工具“五周前还不在任务清单上”，现在却突然成为必须项，显示行业变化之快。

不过，并非所有厂商都完全欢迎。Elektron对“vibe coding”式改装表达复杂态度，禁止其官方论坛链接到破解和修改固件，但并未一般性禁止讨论，理由是担心损坏乐器。其论坛声明警告，修改固件和机器可能导致设备变砖、阻止未来更新并影响保修。尽管如此，Elektron并未积极阻挠改装社区。行业共识是，社区驱动的快速实验性改装已经搅动音乐设备世界，现在无法回头，试图筑墙阻止是错误策略。O’Donnell也表示，把用户隔离开是一场必败之战，因此inMusic选择拥抱社区。这一转向可能推动音乐硬件从封闭产品转向更开放的开发平台，影响现场演出、工作室制作、DIY改装和教育实验等场景，同时也将迫使厂商重新设计保修、安全恢复和官方/社区软件并存的规则。

history.title: How NVIDIA Open Source Tools Are Helping Researchers Build Next-Generation 6G Networks
history.description: A year ago, NVIDIA open sourced its Aerial wireless software, joining Sionna and a broader suite of open source tools for accelerating next-generation 6G network development. Together, they give researchers a foundation for testing ideas, comparing results and building on each other’s work — connecting simulation and AI training with experiments on real over-the-air wireless […]
history.content: A year ago, NVIDIA open sourced its Aerial wireless software, joining Sionna and a broader suite of open source tools for accelerating next-generation 6G network development. Together, they give researchers a foundation for testing ideas, comparing results and building on each other’s work — connecting simulation and AI training with experiments on real over-the-air wireless systems. Today, researchers and developers are using these tools to build 6G-ready networks that do more than just transmit data — receiving signals more effectively, keeping robots and autonomous systems connected when it matters most, and adapting in real time as devices move through the world. Over the past year, global developer adoption of NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna software has grown 10x, while NVIDIA’s open source 5G/6G tools have surpassed 1 million downloads. More than 8,000 research and academic institutions worldwide are using these platforms. The projects emerging today offer a view of how future networks could look. Each addresses a different challenge, but together point toward a broader ambition for building AI-native 6G networks that deliver connectivity, computing and sensing over a converged software-defined platform for billions of people, machines and agents. Networks That Help Robots React Faster A robot picking up an object needs to understand its surroundings and act before they change. When the AI powering that decision runs on a nearby server or in the cloud, the wireless connection becomes part of the response time. Researchers are exploring a more efficient approach called goal-oriented semantic communications. Instead of sending full images, robots transmit compact descriptions of objects, their positions and their relationships. Transmitting just as much information as needed allows robots to more quickly respond, especially in dynamic environments like workplaces and warehouses. At King’s College London, researchers connected a camera-equipped robot arm to an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin running NVIDIA Sionna, which supports both software-defined 5G network and edge AI processing. In fruit-packing and cube-stacking experiments with deliberately introduced faults, the approach reduced robot task completion time by up to 52.6% and improved task success compared with sending periodic images. In addition to quicker responses and less processing overhead, the system also proved more resilient — detecting dropped objects, recovering from unsuccessful actions and, in configurations using a digital twin, checking planned movements for potential collisions before execution. Networks That Learn to Receive Signals Better For a firefighter receiving live drone footage or a rescue team searching for a missing person, timely images can help guide urgent decisions. But interference and changing radio conditions can make wireless signals harder to decode, causing errors and retransmissions that delay information from the field. AI receivers address this challenge by learning to recover information from incoming signals more effectively. Better reception could help responders maintain a clearer, more current view of a fire scene or search area. SoftBank demonstrated this by integrating a neural receiver into NVIDIA Aerial CUDA-Accelerated RAN (ACAR) and testing it with a commercial 5G smartphone. In controlled tests with interference, the neural receiver delivered higher uplink throughput than a conventional receiver at all 15 tested settings, with a maximum gain of roughly 60%. Another way to improve reception is to teach receivers about the environments where they operate. Using NVIDIA Aerial Testbed, ETH Zurich researchers found that tuning neural receivers using local measurements reduced block error rates by more than one-third compared with selected pretrained versions. Networks That Learn When to Save Power As 6G connects more devices and supports more AI applications, managing energy demand will become increasingly important. For example, a network may need enough capacity to serve a busy stadium, but demand changes when the crowd leaves. AI can help identify when spare capacity can power down — and when it needs to come back online — so operators can reduce electricity use without dropping connections. At the University of Leeds, researchers developed a system that predicts network demand 10 minutes ahead and uses those forecasts to guide base station sleep decisions. Before powering down, it checks that neighboring active stations can continue serving affected devices and monitors for changes that require capacity to be restored. The team tested their approach using a portable, NVIDIA DGX Spark-powered 5G “network-in-a-box” alongside a digital twin for validating decisions against real wireless equipment. The result: researchers reported a 45.6% reduction in RAN power consumption relative to a full-power baseline while maintaining device connectivity. Networks That Can Be Tested Faster — Before They’re Built Before deploying a network, researchers need to know how it will perform when hundreds of devices compete for connections or radio signals run into interference. Simulating these conditions helps teams evaluate designs before committing to costly equipment and field trials. But realistic simulations can take hours, limiting how many ideas researchers can explore. The Centre Tecnològic de Telecomunicacions de Catalunya (CTTC) is accelerating that process by bringing GPU-accelerated radio channel models, running on ACAR, into CTTC’s open source 5G-LENA network simulator. These models calculate how wireless signals travel between antennas and devices — a computation that grows increasingly demanding as simulated networks grow. In an early evaluation, the approach reduced simulation runtime from approximately three hours to 10-20 minutes, depending on the integration, while preserving the expected statistical behavior and network performance. Faster simulations let researchers compare more designs, investigate more demanding scenarios and refine ideas sooner. As the industry develops 6G, this could shorten the path from a proposed innovation to a thoroughly evaluated network design — helping teams build better connectivity before deploying it in the real world. At NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C., attend 6G Developer Sessions where researchers and developers will showcase more innovations shaping the future of wireless networks. NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna are available on GitHub.

history.titleZh: NVIDIA 开源工具如何助力研究人员构建下一代 6G 网络
history.descriptionZh:
一年前，NVIDIA 将其 Aerial 无线软件开源，并与 Sionna 及更广泛的开源工具套件一起，为下一代 6G 网络研发提供加速基础。这些工具把仿真、AI 训练与真实空口无线系统实验连接起来，使研究人员能够测试想法、比较结果并在彼此工作基础上继续推进。过去一年，全球开发者对 NVIDIA AI Aerial 和 NVIDIA Sionna 软件的采用量增长 10 倍，NVIDIA 开源 5G/6G 工具下载量超过 100 万次，全球已有 8000 多家研究和学术机构使用这些平台。当前涌现的项目展示了未来网络的可能形态：它们分别解决不同挑战，但共同指向一个更广泛的目标——构建 AI 原生 6G 网络，在融合的软件定义平台上为数十亿人、机器和智能体同时提供连接、计算和感知能力。

在机器人应用方面，研究人员正在探索“目标导向语义通信”。传统方式下，机器人若依赖附近服务器或云端 AI 做决策，无线连接时延会成为响应时间的一部分；新方法不再传输完整图像，而是发送关于物体、位置及其关系的紧凑描述，只传输必要信息，从而加快动态环境中的响应速度。伦敦国王学院将配备摄像头的机械臂连接到运行 NVIDIA Sionna 的 NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin，该系统同时支持软件定义 5G 网络和边缘 AI 处理。在水果包装和方块堆叠实验中，研究人员故意引入故障，结果显示该方法将机器人任务完成时间最多缩短 52.6%，任务成功率也优于周期性发送图像的方式。系统还表现出更强韧性，可检测掉落物体、从失败动作中恢复，并在使用数字孪生的配置中于执行前检查计划运动是否可能碰撞。

在信号接收方面，AI 接收机通过学习更有效地从 incoming 信号中恢复信息，以应对干扰和无线条件变化造成的解码困难、错误和重传。软银将神经接收机集成到 NVIDIA Aerial CUDA 加速 RAN（ACAR）中，并用商用 5G 智能手机测试。在受控干扰测试中，神经接收机在全部 15 个测试设置下的上行吞吐量均高于传统接收机，最大增益约 60%。另一种思路是让接收机学习其所处环境：苏黎世联邦理工学院利用 NVIDIA Aerial Testbed 发现，使用本地测量数据调优神经接收机，相比选定的预训练版本可将块错误率降低三分之一以上。这类更佳接收能力有望帮助消防员和救援团队更清晰、更及时地获取无人机画面或搜索区域信息。

在节能方面，随着 6G 连接更多设备并支持更多 AI 应用，能耗管理将日益重要。网络需要满足体育场等场景的高容量需求，但人群离开后需求会变化。AI 可识别何时可关闭闲置容量、何时需重新上线，从而在不掉线的情况下降低用电。利兹大学开发了一套系统，可提前 10 分钟预测网络需求，并用预测指导基站休眠决策；休眠前会检查邻近活跃基站能否继续服务受影响设备，并监测需要恢复容量的变化。团队使用由 NVIDIA DGX Spark 驱动的便携式 5G“network-in-a-box”以及数字孪生，在真实无线设备上验证决策。结果显示，相对于全功率基线，RAN 功耗降低 45.6%，同时保持设备连接。

在网络仿真与部署前验证方面，研究人员需要了解数百台设备竞争连接或信号遇到干扰时的网络表现。真实感仿真可帮助团队在投入昂贵设备和现场试验前评估设计，但往往耗时数小时，限制可探索的想法数量。加泰罗尼亚电信技术中心（CTTC）将运行在 ACAR 上的 GPU 加速无线信道模型引入其开源 5G-LENA 网络仿真器。这些模型计算无线信号在天线与设备间的传播，随着仿真网络规模增大，计算需求也日益提高。早期评估显示，该方法将仿真运行时间从约 3 小时缩短至 10—20 分钟（取决于集成方式），同时保持预期的统计行为和网络性能。更快仿真使研究人员能比较更多设计、研究更苛刻场景并更早完善想法，有望缩短从提出创新到完成全面评估网络设计的路径，帮助团队在真实部署前构建更好的连接能力。

总体来看，这些项目覆盖机器人实时响应、AI 神经接收、智能节能和高效仿真验证等 6G 关键方向，体现了开源工具在连接仿真、AI 训练与真实无线实验方面的作用。NVIDIA 表示，AI Aerial 和 Sionna 已在 GitHub 上提供，并将在华盛顿特区 GTC 的 6G Developer Sessions 上展示更多塑造未来无线网络的创新。

history.title: GlobalFoundries VP details FDX Fusion technology, sporting 7nm-class performance without the need for EUV tools — company targets 2030 for high-volume manufacturing, with planar transistors in tow
history.description: GlobalFoundries reveals new details about its FDX Fusion technology, which promises 7nm-class performance and 8nm-class logic density using planar FD-SOI transistors without EUV lithography, shares what is next for FDX Fusion node, and the FDX program in general.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Eight years after GlobalFoundries abandoned the development of its 7nm FinFET technology, the company is preparing to return to 7nm-class performance, this time by going via a different route. Its FDX Fusion process, built on FD-SOI (fully depleted silicon-on-insulator) technology, promises 7nm-class performance using advanced planar transistors, with no EUV lithography necessary.In an interview with Tom's Hardware Premium, GlobalFoundries' Sudipto Bose, vice president of the FD-SOI business unit, shared new details about its FDX Fusion technology, including its 8nm-class logic density, advanced planar transistors, manufacturing costs, and plans to begin commercial production in 2028. The company also explained how it intends to compete with conventional FinFET technologies and why it believes FD-SOI has a future beyond the 22nm-class generation. Some elements of this interview transcript have been edited for flow and clarity.Sudipto Bose: I have been at GlobalFoundries (GF) for a little bit over six years, and I have been in the industry for 25+ years. I spent the rest of my career at Texas Instruments (TI), so it's really two jobs that I have done: TI and GF. Half and half engineering and business. I spent a lot of my business days in the automotive segment. This was what I was doing at GF when I joined, and now I have the FDX product line role.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Sudipto Bose: A little bit on the history of FDX at GF. GF has been investing in FD-SOI for a long time. It started [these efforts] before I joined. So I would say almost eight years now. And a lot of the investment thesis that drove us towards FDX Fusion is based on the traction that we have in the market today, right? We have quite a few customers who are ramping up. And I say quite a few; this is like high double-digit customers in the nineties that are ramping up right now.Applications for FDX Fusion Anton Shilov: What specific types of chips and devices is FDX Fusion designed for? Which application will benefit most from its capabilities? You may like GlobalFoundries unveils 7nm-class FDX Fusion node — comes 7 years after firm abandoned FinFET China crafts working 3nm gate-all-around transistors without EUV Analyzing Intel's EMIB and Foveros advanced packaging roadmaps Sudipto Bose: FDX Fusion will try to enhance the applications in which we play today. What do I mean by that? If you look at our current customers, they are designing chips, everything to do with connectivity. When I say connectivity, think of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, satcom, all of that. So that is one class of customers.There's another class of customers who are designing processors at the edge, so these are MCUs (microcontroller units) with some level of inference sitting inside. Think of customers like Alif Semiconductors. So that is another class: MCUs at the edge.Then in automotive, we have a disproportionate exposure to radar, and this is because of the eighty-one gigahertz performance that FDX brings to the table. So we will engage with them as they try to enhance their portfolio. We also have an automotive MCU, but radar is where you will see a lot of press releases that we have done.Last but not least, we also have exposure in the data center segment. This also goes back to the fT/fmax, the high-performance RF that we have, which is a good candidate for designing TIAs and clock recovery circuits. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Anton Shilov: By applications inside data centers, what exactly do you mean? CPUs? What to read next Samsung's fab roadmaps examined Intel 14A moves closer to production as PDK 0.9 becomes available The ABF substrate data center roadmap — solving the supply crunch and material wall beneath every AI accelerator Sudipto Bose: Not CPUs. It is in the connectivity space. So, if you think about GF's focus, we are very focused on two things in data centers: power and connectivity. So in the connectivity space, we have silicon photonics, or turning electrons into photons. But then when you receive them, you have the optical diode, again, a GF silicon photonics technology. After that, you need circuits that will amplify those weak electrical signals and drive them to the compute chip. This circuit, which amplifies the weak electrical signals, is right now being done by GF silicon-germanium, but once FDX Fusion is there, we'll offer them both [as] options. And so, to be very specific to your answer, these are data/signal paths inside the data center that feed into CPUs.7nm-class FD-SOI nodeGlobalFoundries' FDX Fusion is a new manufacturing technology that promises 8nm-class logic density and 7nm-class power and performance without EUV lithography or FinFET transistors, which greatly reduces design costs and manufacturing costs at the cost of significantly lower transistor density compared to 7nm-class nodes. Instead, the process relies on advanced planar fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) transistors, strained silicon substrates, and aggressive optical patterning techniques to achieve transistor dimensions comparable to those of conventional 8nm-class FinFET nodes. FDX Fusion also retains support for adaptive body biasing and combines high-density digital logic with RF, analog, and embedded memory capabilities. The technology will be manufactured using deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography, although its tighter gate and metal pitches will likely require extensive multipatterning for the most critical layers.Anton Shilov: What are the key innovations of FDX Fusion compared to predecessors and other nodes that are currently used?Sudipto Bose: The key things that we're improving from the current-generation FDX, the first one is fT/fmax, this is 500 GHz, or 0.5 THz fT/fmax. This helps the first segment that I talked about, which is connectivity. This helps automotive radar, and this definitely helps the data center segment as they try to improve data speeds. So this is not really competing with silicon germanium. Think of it as silicon germanium at the very high end, and FDX in the 100 – 200 Gb per lambda space. That is one. The second one is the inference at the edge. So we can call it physical AI, and we look at physical AI as sense, think, act, and connect. But the kind of feature set we are putting in starts with improving the digital gate density. This is 2.2 times more dense than the current generation FDX (22FDX and 22FDX+). (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Sudipto Bose: We are putting in a lot of flavors of eNVM, a lot of flavors of SRAM, because in edge AI, and in fact for any AI, the real game is how much memory you can pack without increasing the cost. So we are adding a lot of flavors of those. The way we architected FDX Fusion is that we set a goal of how much performance we can deliver to our customer base without increasing their operating expenses.If you look at classic 7nm, 6nm, they require EUV tools. The mask set is costly; the tool chain is costly. The FDX Fusion platform that we've built isn't going to use EUV tools. It is also based on planar technology. So there are two advantages to this. One is that we can support a much more competitive mask set price compared to 6nm. We can also offer [customers] a lot more flexibility in terms of cycle time and in how many places we manufacture, because FDX Fusion does not need EUV tools.So, to summarize the answer? We are trying to improve RF and analog performance, digital gate density, and the classes of memory that we offer. What applications are we trying to target? It is connectivity, edge AI, high-frequency mmWave, automotive radar, and definitely applications inside data centers. Could you share any numbers?Sudipto Bose: I will share a number with you. But I will also give you a little bit of context on how our customers look at our technology portfolio. If you look at the current generation, the one that we are manufacturing today, the one where I said we have 90+ customers ramping. Not designing, ramping. This basically comes from the flexibility of FD-SOI. You have the box, the depleted channel, and you can use body bias. So we have customers who are able to achieve 16nm-class power and performance with 22FDX. What do I mean by 16nm-class power and performance?It essentially means that although our gate density is not as close to 16mm, when you look at the system-level requirements like CPU clock, but think of it as TOPS per watt, we are matching 16nm; in some cases, we are matching 12nm-class.[...] If I were sitting in a time machine and went back seven years, instead of calling it 22FDX, we could have called it 16FDX, right? Or we could have called it 16nm-class FDX. So with that analogy, if you come to FDX Fusion, our gate density of FDX Fusion will be exactly the same as the industry's 8nm standard today.It is 14 million gates per square millimeter; that is the density.Note: Assuming he uses a two-input NAND gate as its reference, each gate contains four transistors, which translates to 56 MTr/mm², which is comparable to what Samsung's 8nm-class nodes use.Sudipto Bose: Now, why do we call it 7nm-class? Or we actually thought of calling it 6nm-class, but then we said, let's wait for some silicon before we go too far ahead. It is because digital gate density is one aspect of a solution. It defines your physical size, the die size, and that is great. But then you need power and performance. And with the adaptive body bias (ABB) capability that FD-SOI has, and with the standard cell metallization innovations that we have brought in FDX Fusion, once a device is done and you again look at TOPS per watt, it should be equivalent, if not better, than what 7nm can achieve. That is our product target. So for a customer, the value it brings [customers] is: 'I do not have to use an EUV tool line. I do not have to use a mask set that costs many millions of dollars.'I have something which costs a few millions of dollars, has great cycle time, but at the same time, I am getting TOPS per watt, which is similar to or better than 7nm. The die size might be bigger, but again, it should not be no bigger than what 8nm is today. And that is the messaging to the industry; that is why we say 7nm-class instead of saying, 'Hey, this is 7nm density.' We are trying to reflect what our customers have told us. That in the edge world, in the physical AI world, the size of the die is one aspect, but if the die does not meet the power requirement of the application, then the whole system will not function. So that is the push.Anton Shilov: That is perhaps why you actually called the technology FDX Fusion instead of using some fancy number.Sudipto Bose: Yes, because the moment we put a number [out], people put us in a box. And we want to give customers the optionality of, 'Listen, you want to design a transimpedance amplifier using the fT/fmax that we have? That's an analog circuit. No one cares about digital gate density. Go build it.''You want to build a simple MCU, which is just SRAM and IOs? We have 14 million gates per square millimeter. Go build it.' 'You want to build a mixed-signal design like a single-chip radar, Wi-Fi, a satcom digital beamformer? Here are the few other knobs that you can turn to get the best PPA or the best system performance that you need.'That is why we chose the name Fusion; we are trying to imply [that] we give you many options. It is the combination of all the good things the world needs to design the physical AI dream that we have put in front of ourselves, like the whole stack concept of 'sense, think, act, and connect'. Let us see if it sticks. I think it is a bold move for us to go against the grain of the way the foundry industry typically names its platforms, but we feel pretty strong about it.Anton Shilov: So, you shared the gate density number, but could you maybe also share things like contacted gate pitch, metal pitch as well?Sudipto Bose: In time. The reason I mention that is there is a little bit of IP involved. We want to get the first silicon out, engage with a few customers before we publish the CPP and the M(etal) layers. […] We are pushing the limits of patterning and coloring as well as gate oxide engineering to get the best CPP and metal pitches, which will enable this level of density of gates. That is, I would say in terms of R&D dollars just at a very high level, 50% of R&D dollars is on the transistor itself because we are doing strained substrates. There are multiple techniques we are using to improve the PFET and NFET performance. The other 50% is all on CPP and metal pitches.Anton Shilov: So, are those contacted gate pitches and metal pitches comparable to conventional 7nm class FinFET process technologies?Sudipto Bose: Comparable to 8nm.Anton Shilov: When we talk about 8nm, basically speaking, there is only one company that actually produces chips using an 8nm-class technology. That is Samsung Foundry. TSMC and Intel Foundry do not have 8nm-class technologies. So I suppose that we should compare it to Samsung's 8nm node, right?Sudipto Bose: That's a fair guess.Anton Shilov: When it comes to power consumption improvements versus 22FDX and 22FDX+, how much lower power can we get using the new FDX Fusion node?Sudipto Bose: It depends on the application, but I understand your question. So if you just normalize with [iso performance and iso power], I am giving you an answer with adaptive body bias included. If you consider current-generation FDX as the base point, the goal of FDX Fusion is to get 30% higher performance and 40% lower power. Again, it is really application-driven [in] how low you can go. But if you take the standard core, our goal is to get at least a 20% improvement.Anton Shilov: What types of chips do you expect to benefit most from the FDX Fusion technology? You mentioned connectivity, edge AI, high RF, automotive radar, and connectivity applications inside data centers. What about application-specific AI accelerators, because you mentioned edge inference?Sudipto Bose: From the STAC — sense, think, act, and connect — framework point of view, let me give you an example. Think of a humanoid, or a car — major applications that need to see. It needs to see and then infer what the environment is like. So the class of chips that do this vision processing at the edge to infer the surroundings will definitely be supported with FDX Fusion. The class of chips that will hear, do voice recognition, and, from voice recognition, draw conclusions, we definitely want to support [them]. Now, at the data center right now, as I said, our play is connectivity. Just translating optical to electrical signals.If a customer wants to use a chiplet, which has a lot of memory, think of analog in-memory compute along with an inference engine, by all means we will support [such applications]. We will work with customers to see how we can play in that compute ecosystem in the data center. But in terms of pure focus, the first 10 customers that we are engaged with are either at the edge, or they are in the connectivity piece inside the data center.Note: For those of our readers who are not familiar with ABB, this is a technique that dynamically adjusts a transistor's threshold voltage by changing the voltage applied to the transistor body. Forward body bias reduces threshold voltage to improve performance, while reverse body bias increases it to reduce power leakage. This enables chips to optimize performance and power consumption according to workload requirements. ABB is one of the key advantages of the FD-SOI technology.Anton Shilov: Since you mentioned this, does FDX Fusion retain the active body biasing capabilities of its predecessors?Sudipto Bose: It is an inseparable part of the platform, yes. We will launch this platform in a way that customers can use it.New tools requiredAnton Shilov: You also mentioned makers of wafer fab equipment. Will FDX Fusion use existing manufacturing equipment at the Dresden facility, or will it require substantial investments in new lithography, deposition, etching, and metrology tools?Sudipto Bose: It will require new tools. Substantial is a relative term. If you see the amount of money being invested in semiconductors, the term 'substantial' has changed. We are going to get new tools, which is why we combined the FDX Fusion announcement event with the topping off of the Sprint expansion project. That's why we had all the luminaries from the German and the European government. There will be tool investment; we will be buying tools from the vendors. How much of it is going to be litho versus etching? Time will tell, but for sure we need new tools compared to what we have today. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Anton Shilov: But will you essentially need to completely re-equip the Dresden facility to use FDX Fusion? What percentage of the tools you have can be reused for FDX Fusion?Sudipto Bose: We can get back to you on that exact answer because I do want to give you a proper answer, rather than a high-level answer. But I will tell you where the targets are. With the front end, the transistor fabrication tool chain, my target is to reuse as much as we can.Anton Shilov: You also mentioned that you plan to begin manufacturing FDX Fusion in 2028. But does this refer to risk production, initial customer production, or high volume manufacturing?Sudipto Bose: Initial customer production.Anton Shilov: When do you expect the technology to reach mature yields and meaningful production volumes?Sudipto Bose: I will give you my target, and then the industry will define it because we are a part of a bigger ecosystem. 2030 is when we want to get to high-volume manufacturing with FDX Fusion. But again, it depends on the first applications and the first few customers. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Readiness Anton Shilov: Speaking of customers, you probably already have customers who are committed to production, haven't you?Sudipto Bose: We have customers who are committed to building a chip. Of course, we have to deliver to their specs before they go to production.Anton Shilov: I suppose the customers that you mentioned in the press release like BMW, Bosch NXP, Siemens, and Tesla, they are all plan to build chips on this technology.Sudipto Bose: […] They have been pushing us for the last few years to do something like this, and they have given us requirements. Now we are doing it, and we have to show them what we can [deliver]. So there is a lot of push that we have received from the industry, from these companies. When I say these companies, the supply chain that leads into these companies to deliver something which will work at the edge. So we are racing against time to show them something that will meet the specs.Anton Shilov: GlobalFoundries plans to release the initial FDX Fusion PDK in mid-2027. But when do you expect complete digital, analog, and RF design flows to become available from the three major EDA vendors?Sudipto Bose: Yeah. I wish I could tell you… Right now we are in discussion with all the major primes, so we are in the request for information/request for quotation (RFI/RFQ) phase, but we have started discussions with the major EDA vendors. It has been almost six to nine months now.Anton Shilov: But you do expect all the leading EDA vendors to support FDX Fusion in eight to nine months?Sudipto Bose: Of course. We are going to engage with the whole ecosystem that we have, and once [the PDK is out], we have to support a proper flow not just for chip design, but also IPs that are required and everything else around it.Anton Shilov: So how extensive will the initial FDX Fusion IP ecosystem be? Will customers have access to silicon-proven standard cell libraries, SRAM compilers, embedded non-volatile memory, interface IPs, maybe analog and radio frequency building blocks before 2028?Sudipto Bose: Yes. In the first two years, we are going to engage with pilot customers. Think of these as early adopters. We have early adopters listed, and we will design standard cell, I/Os, and SRAM [...] needed for everything, so we will have those. But then the complex IPs, like PCIe Gen 4/5 or LPDDR6 or a DisplayPort, will be dictated by the first few applications that will ramp. FDX Fusion for us is the beginning of a journey. We have been on the journey of 22FDX for almost eight years. I envision FDX Fusion to be more than that. Even on our current platforms, we keep enhancing our IP portfolio. So I expect us to be adding IPs to FDX Fusion over the next ten years. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)ARC, MIPS, and Fusion FDXAnton Shilov: GlobalFoundries also highlighted its ARC and MIPS processor IP portfolios and RISC-V expertise as part of the FDX Fusion offering. Do you plan to develop processor cores and AI accelerators specifically optimized for FDX Fusion? IPs specifically optimized for FDX Fusion? Or will you primarily port existing IP to the new process?Sudipto Bose: MIPS is an internal customer and a partner, and we will engage with them, and they will launch a platform for physical AI that is fine-tuned, in a combination of what they have and what FDX Fusion has. ARC and MIPS are key pieces of the strategy. Having an internal customer like that just enhances our development cycle by 5X because now they can start developing fast turns of test chips and give us feedback. We did not have this capability in the past. Now we do. Once they are ready, they will start announcing stuff.Anton Shilov: So essentially, you will both port the existing IPs to the new node, but also MIPS will likely develop something brand new specifically for FDX Fusion.Sudipto Bose: Yes.Costs Anton Shilov: How will the manufacturing complexity and cost per transistor of FDX Fusion compare to 22FDX+, your 12nm FinFET technology, and conventional 8nm FinFET technology?Sudipto Bose: This would be the most advanced planar transistor that the world has seen, the most advanced non-EUV-based manufacturing line that the world has seen. So, I would say significantly more complex than our current 22nm-class FD-SOI line. More complex than what we have on the 12nm FinFET line. We are working with every tool vendor that you can think of as part of this program, and we have given them the challenges. It goes back to your question about our contacted gate pitch and metal pitch. So, we have had multiple workshops with them over the last few quarters, and each one of them is proposing a tool recipe that they think will get this to a nice and solid yield. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Sudipto Bose: So, I guess the answer to your question is: firstly, it is definitely complex, and secondly, we are really using the entire ecosystem available to us to come up with tool configurations that will deliver this. All of this is going to happen in Dresden. We have to be competitive, so price is always dictated by the market. Our goal is to have a running cost that is significantly better than a 7nm or a 6nm class of design (due to planar transistors and due to lack of EUV masks). After that, we will work with our customers to figure out what makes sense. But you are right, the value that we want to bring in is, 'dear customers, you do not have the same operating expenses load, meaning the cost of tape-out is less than 6nm.'And you can do multiple tape-outs because this class of devices is not something where you can design one part and use it for 15 applications. You really need 15 devices for 15 applications. So, we definitely enable that. Then, when it comes to manufacturing cost, it is a discussion with our customers. We have various business models, but the goal is to make sure it is a win-win. At the end of the day, the lower the cost we are, the more flexibility we can provide to our customers. The non-EUV path is one of the things that was dictated by our decision that we must keep this a cost-competitive platform.Anton Shilov: So, cost-wise you want to be competitive, but it's likely comparable to 8nm.Sudipto Bose: I will have a better feel once we are complete with what we call our M-cycles inside the fab. But I would say my internal target is that we have to be better than that.The future of FDX Anton Shilov: GlobalFoundries describes upcoming technology as its 1st Generation of FDX Fusion. Does this mean that you envision subsequent generations with high transistor density and performance? Maybe you can share some preliminary targets or timelines for the next node?Sudipto Bose: We have listed quite a few innovation steps that we want to enable on this platform. The FDX Fusion definition is based on the ones we believe we are more confident that we will be able to deliver in the timeframe that we have said. We have kept a few things in the innovation lab, and they are pushing the boundaries of a few things like eNVM, EDA routing, chip folding, 2.5D integration, which, once they mature, will define what the next version of FDX Fusion will look like. I do not have a timeline for the next version of FDX Fusion, though.As we proceed through the development phase, I would say early 2028 to mid-2028 is when I expect to have a better view of when the next version will be launched. And this is also based on feedback we will get from customers. Because what we have right now is our first silicon, which is running in the lab, which we will show to customers. They will give us a lot of feedback. I am sure we will get a few things right, and at the same time, we will get a few things not so right. And that feedback, along with a few of the innovation topics I mentioned, will dictate what the next generation is going to look like. Stay tuned! (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Anton Shilov: One of the reasons why I aksed about next-generation nodes is partly because TSMC typically shares its process technology roadmaps with new nodes well before it releases early PDKs for these nodes. Given that FDX Fusion is now GF's most advanced logic process, with capabilities comparable to 8nm-class technologies (i.e., more advanced than 22FDX or bulk 12nm FinFET), how frequently does GlobalFoundries plan to introduce new process technologies, and how far in advance will it disclose its roadmap?Sudipto Bose: I would say, we are doing advanced development across the board. If you look at the work we are doing on silicon photonics, on packaging, on power transistors like GaN, RF GaN, Power GaN, these are all pretty advanced. But yes, you are right: in what the world understands as a classic, let's say, high-density process, FDX Fusion is the most advanced. We typically announce or update the industry about our roadmap every year at the GlobalFoundries Technology Symposium. Like this year at GTS, we announced FDX Fusion. So, I would say stay tuned for the GTS sessions that we have, and typically every year we do it in September or October.CEA-Leti involvement Anton Shilov: CEA-Leti describes FDX Fusion as a single-digit FD-SOI node. How closely is this new technology related to CEA-Leti's own research in 10nm and 7nm with their SOI nodes?Sudipto Bose: The platform that we have right now is the outside of the substrate engineering work that we are doing with Soitec and CEA-Leti; the rest of it is GF inherent IP at this point in time. So we are bringing in the knowledge that we have from current-generation FDX, the knowledge that we have from the work that we did in 7nm before we stopped it, the work that we have done on 12nm. So it is bringing in all the innovations across all the GF fabs to figure out what is the best that we can offer. Does it mean that we will not look at what CEA-Leti has in the future? I do not have an answer right now. But for now, FDX Fusion is a very GF innovation-driven effort. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)Anton Shilov: So you did not use pre-competitive IP from CEA-Leti to develop FDX Fusion? Is it a completely internally developed node?Sudipto Bose: Correct.Anton Shilov: The press release mentions innovations in substrate engineering along with endorsements from CEA-Leti and Soitec. What exactly does that involve, and how does it improve transistor performance? What role do Soitec and CEA-Leti play in developing FDX's strained silicon substrates, and how close is this technology to mass production?Sudipto Bose: GlobalFoundries is working with CEA-Leti and Soitec under the FAMES program to develop strained silicon substrates for FDX Fusion. The goal is to improve charge carrier mobility and, consequently, transistor performance. Since FD-SOI technology relies on specialized silicon-on-insulator wafers supplied by Soitec, the three organizations are developing ways to introduce strain into these substrates and make the technology suitable for high-volume manufacturing. The approach has already demonstrated its viability in the laboratory, and the partners are now refining the manufacturing process to prepare it for commercial production.[Session ends]

history.titleZh: 格芯副总裁详解FDX Fusion技术：无需EUV工具即可实现7nm级性能——公司目标2030年大规模量产，并采用平面晶体管
history.descriptionZh:
GlobalFoundries在约八年前放弃7nm FinFET研发后，正计划以另一条技术路线重返7nm级性能：基于FD-SOI（全耗尽绝缘体上硅）的FDX Fusion工艺。该平台采用先进平面晶体管，不依赖EUV光刻，目标是在2028年进入初始客户生产、2030年实现高量产，并提供8nm级逻辑密度和7nm级功耗性能。GlobalFoundries FD-SOI业务部门副总裁Sudipto Bose在接受Tom's Hardware采访时披露了该工艺的密度、成本、IP生态、制造安排和客户进展。

背景上，GlobalFoundries长期投资FD-SOI，现有22FDX/22FDX+平台已有90多家客户处于量产爬坡阶段，覆盖连接、边缘MCU、汽车雷达和数据中心连接等。公司称，正是这些客户对边缘物理AI和低成本先进节点的需求，推动其开发FDX Fusion。BMW、Bosch、NXP、Siemens、Tesla等汽车与工业链企业过去几年持续施压并提出规格要求。GlobalFoundries还拥有ARC、MIPS和RISC-V相关处理器IP，MIPS作为内部客户和合作伙伴将推出面向物理AI的平台，以加速测试芯片和反馈循环。

核心技术原理方面，FDX Fusion不是FinFET，而是先进平面FD-SOI晶体管，保留FD-SOI的关键能力——自适应体偏置（ABB）。ABB通过调节晶体管体端电压动态改变阈值电压：正体偏置降低阈值电压以提升性能，反体偏置提高阈值电压以降低漏电，从而按负载优化功耗和性能。FDX Fusion还采用应变硅衬底、栅氧工程以及激进的光学图形化/多重曝光技术，用DUV实现更紧的栅极和金属间距。由于不使用EUV，掩膜组成本显著低于6nm/7nm，工具链和晶圆厂选择也更灵活，但关键层需要大量多重图形化。GlobalFoundries与Soitec、CEA-Leti在FAMES计划下开发应变SOI衬底，以提高载流子迁移率和晶体管性能；该衬底方案已在实验室验证可行，正在优化量产工艺。公司强调，除衬底工程合作外，FDX Fusion主要是GlobalFoundries自有IP，未使用CEA-Leti的预竞争IP。

性能参数上，FDX Fusion的逻辑密度为每平方毫米1400万门；若以二输入NAND每门4个晶体管换算，约合56 MTr/mm²，与三星8nm级工艺相当，是22FDX的2倍以上。GlobalFoundries称其接触栅间距和金属间距与8nm级相当，但不愿在首批硅出来前公布具体CPP和金属间距。与22FDX相比，在开启ABB、等性能条件下功耗可降低40%，等功耗条件下性能提升30%；标准核心目标至少提升20%。与12LP+相比，性能提升16%、功耗降低20%，密度为56对30–40 MTr/mm²。与7nm相比，在ABB开启条件下性能约高4%、功耗约低5%，但晶体管密度明显更低（56对约91.2 MTr/mm²）；与三星8LPP相比密度为56对约61.2 MTr/mm²。其fT/fmax达到500GHz，强化了射频和毫米波能力，包括81GHz汽车雷达。公司将其定位为“7nm级”而非“7nm密度”，因为边缘物理AI更看重TOPS/W、内存容量和系统功耗，芯片面积可大于7nm但不会大于8nm。

应用场景包括：Wi-Fi、蓝牙、蜂窝、卫星通信等连接芯片；带推理能力的边缘MCU；汽车雷达和汽车MCU；数据中心内的连接链路，如硅光子接收后的跨阻放大器、时钟恢复电路，而不是CPU。FDX Fusion还面向视觉处理、语音识别、单芯片雷达、卫星通信数字波束成形、混合信号设计，以及未来可能的chiplet和模拟存内计算。公司提出“感知、思考、行动、连接”的物理AI框架，首批10家合作客户集中在边缘或数据中心连接。

制造与生态方面，FDX Fusion将在德国德累斯顿生产，需要新增设备，但前端晶体管工具链尽量复用现有设备，具体复用比例未披露。工艺复杂性显著高于22FDX和12nm FinFET，公司正与多家设备商合作开发工具配方。初始客户生产目标为2028年，高量产目标为2030年；2027年中发布初始PDK。EDA方面，公司正与主要厂商进行RFI/RFQ沟通，预计完整数字、模拟和RF流程将获支持。初期IP生态包括标准单元、I/O、SRAM及多种eNVM，复杂接口IP如PCIe Gen4/5、LPDDR6、DisplayPort将由首批量产应用决定，并计划未来十年持续扩展。成本上，公司目标使运行成本显著优于7nm/6nm级设计，内部目标甚至优于8nm级；但每晶体管制造复杂性高于现有22FDX和12nm FinFET。

总体看，FDX Fusion是GlobalFoundries避开EUV和FinFET高成本路线、以FD-SOI平面工艺服务边缘AI、连接、汽车雷达和数据中心连接的战略产品。它不以最高晶体管密度竞争，而是以射频/模拟性能、ABB灵活性、较低掩膜成本和非EUV供应链为卖点。若2028年客户生产和2030年高量产按计划推进，该平台将为欧洲先进逻辑产能和物理AI边缘芯片提供一条差异化路径，但其密度仍落后于7nm FinFET，且EDA、IP和制造良率仍需验证。

history.description: The protesters stormed over the walls and took over the construction site, with the Stop Dirty Data Centers coalition saying that more actions are planned across Europe.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 12 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A Microsoft data center under construction in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, has been overrun by about a hundred protesters, with some carrying placards saying, “Screw your data center.” According to Reuters, the “Stop Dirty Data Centers” coalition is planning actions across 16 countries on November 6 and 7, 2026, including Amsterdam, Dublin, Warsaw, and another Microsoft site in Denmark.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsiblePure Data Centers, which owns the Amsterdam data center, said, “We respectfully ask those on site to leave safely and engage with us in dialogue about the development and any concerns they may have.” The report also quoted Microsoft saying that it understood the strong feeling that people have and respected their right to peaceful expression but says that it does not condone any unlawful action."On 6-7 November 2026 we are taking action across Europe to say Stop Dirty Data Centres," the group's website reads. "Local communities are rising up to stop dirty data centres where they live. We will unite and exercise our democratic rights to speak out, assemble, and protest to hold elected officials to account. We’re calling for an immediate moratorium on large data centres in Europe!" A map on the site shows actions planned at 85 locations across Europe over the coming days.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The group cited a list of concerns about "the explosion of AI data centres across our towns and cities," and claims to be joining to prevent "the irreparable harms data centres pose to the wellbeing of people and planet." They cite local communities, jobs, housing shortages and rising energy bills, the climate crisis, heatwaves and water shortages, big tech undermining democracies, the mental health crisis, increased surveillance and the erosion of privacy, securitization and militarization, and a toxic supply chain as motivations.Data center opposition is one of the issues that has taken center stage in the U.S. midterm elections, with Americans overwhelmingly voting against them. It seems that resistance isn’t limited to the United States, though, as European countries take measures to limit their unlimited development. For example, Google has been hit with a criminal probe after its Finnish subsidiary, Tuike Finland Oy, allegedly destroyed 816 acres of forest without a permit. Denmark has also hit the brakes on data center grid connection requests as total applications exceed 60GW, more than eight times the country’s current peak power consumption. One Italian council also a 200% tax on data center development in agricultural land to encourage developers to reuse old industrial areas instead. history.titleZh: 抗议者冲击微软AI数据中心建设工地
history.descriptionZh:
据Tom's Hardware报道，荷兰阿姆斯特丹一座在建的微软数据中心被约百名抗议者涌入，部分抗议者举着“Screw your data center”（去你的数据中心）等标语。活动由“Stop Dirty Data Centers”联盟组织，计划于2026年11月6日至7日在16个国家同步采取行动，地点包括阿姆斯特丹、都柏林、华沙以及丹麦的另一处微软数据中心；该联盟网站地图显示，未来数日欧洲将有85个地点举行相关行动。数据中心所有者Pure Data Centers表示，尊重现场人员表达诉求，但“请现场人员安全离开，并就项目开发和关切与我们对话”。微软称理解公众的强烈情绪、尊重和平表达权利，但不纵容任何违法行为。

该联盟呼吁“立即暂停欧洲大型数据中心建设”，称AI数据中心在城镇和城市中“爆炸式扩张”，可能对人和地球的福祉造成“不可修复的伤害”。其列出的关切包括：本地社区受影响、就业与住房短缺、能源账单上涨、气候危机、热浪和水资源短缺、大型科技公司削弱民主、心理健康危机、监控增加与隐私侵蚀、安全化与军事化，以及有毒供应链。联盟表示，它并不反对进步，也不要求关闭现有项目，而是希望在各国政府建立更清晰的开发规则之前，暂缓新建AI数据中心，以免对环境和周边居民造成负面影响。

这一抗议反映出AI算力基础设施扩张正遭遇“社会许可”和监管阻力。数据中心是AI模型训练和推理的底层基础设施，通常具有高功率密度、高耗电、高冷却和水资源需求，并需要大规模电网接入和土地审批。争议核心并非反对AI技术本身，而是AI数据中心建设速度超过了能源、土地、环境与地方治理的承载能力。相关事件可能推高云与AI基础设施项目的延迟和合规成本，影响微软等公司的算力部署节奏，也会推动行业更重视旧工业区复用、高效冷却、可再生能源配套和社区协商。

类似阻力正在欧洲多地出现。芬兰方面，谷歌子公司Tuike Finland Oy被指无证毁坏816英亩森林，已遭刑事调查。丹麦因数据中心并网申请总量超过60GW——超过该国当前峰值用电量的8倍——已暂停受理相关并网请求。意大利一个地方议会则对农业用地上的数据中心开发设置200%税率，以鼓励开发商再利用旧工业区。欧盟科技主管Henna Virkkunen表示，AI是非常重要的技术，欧洲需要拥有自己的算力能力，但“对公民而言，非常重要的是他们能相信能源账单不会因数据中心而飙升，不会出现停电，也不会因这些项目破坏环境”。

在美国，数据中心反对已成为中期选举议题之一，文章称美国人以压倒性多数投票反对相关项目，表明阻力并不局限于美国。整体看，这篇新闻不涉及具体AI芯片架构或性能参数，而是聚焦AI数据中心扩张引发的能源、环境、隐私和地方治理冲突；其影响在于，AI基础设施的竞争不仅取决于芯片和资本，也取决于电网接入、环境审批、社区接受度和监管确定性。

history.title: Nvidia tightens tracking of AI GPUs in Southeast Asia as Chinese chip smuggling draws scrutiny, report claims
history.description: Nvidia is requiring Southeast Asian cloud providers seeking Nvidia Cloud Partner status to enroll in its Fleet Intelligence tracking program, giving the chipmaker greater visibility into where its AI GPUs are deployed. The move comes as Washington increases pressure over suspected chip smuggling into China, with investigations involving Megaspeed International and Super Micro highlighting the challenges of enforcing U.S. export restrictions
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Southeast Asia computing providers are now reportedly required to register with Nvidia's Fleet Intelligence tracking system if they want to become official Nvidia Cloud Partners (NCPs). The move, according to Bloomberg, is aimed at giving the chipmaker another way to monitor where its AI accelerators are deployed, as Washington grows increasingly frustrated with restricted hardware finding its way into China through regional smuggling networks. Nvidia was not immediately available for comment.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedThe NCP designation is worth pursuing as it gives cloud providers Nvidia's public endorsement and preferred access to its sought-after AI chips, putting the company in a position to use those benefits as leverage. Customers seeking the status must now enroll in Fleet Intelligence, according to people familiar with the new requirements. Fleet Management was introduced last December primarily as a data centre management tool. It gathers information about NVIDIA hardware deployed across participating companies' infrastructure, including the locations of individual accelerators. That information could give Nvidia a better picture of whether its chips are operating after they leave the supply chain.The system is, however, a universal tracking mandate. Participation has remained voluntary outside the NCP requirement, and Nvidia does not automatically receive location data from every customer using the software. The company has also not clarified whether existing Cloud Partners will have to enroll to retain their designation or whether the requirement will eventually extend beyond Southeast Asia.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Notably, Nvidia has been developing a way to locate AI for some time now. Last December, we reported that the company had developed software-based GPU tracking, using GPU telemetry and network latency measurements to estimate where processors are operating. Nvidia described the software as a customer-installed agent for monitoring hardware health, integrity and inventory.The technology has an obvious use beyond data maintenance. The U.S. restricts Chinese companies from purchasing advanced AI accelerators without a license, yet authorities believe billions of dollars worth of the hardware have reached Chinese buyers through third-party networks, with Southeast Asia becoming an important transit point for those transactions. You may like Investigative report details how export-restricted Nvidia AI chips reach China Nvidia tells data center operators to limit business from Chinese customers with new global restrictions, report claims Illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs found inside state-owned China Telecom's network A C4ADS investigation has previously identified several routes used to move restricted processors into China, including purchases through research initiatives, shell companies and shipments routed through other Southeast Asian countries. The nonprofit examined transactions between 2022 and 2025 and identified $13.4 million worth of Nvidia A100, H100, and AD102-series GPUs moving through regional trade routes. Its report also linked $4.6 billion in hardware purchases to Singapore-based Megaspeed International.Megaspeed has become a particularly awkward case for Nvidia, with the company being under U.S. and Singaporean investigation for more than a year over suspected chip diversion. Last week, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang defended his dealings with the firm, describing them as “completely normal,” adding, “we’ve studied all their deployments of our GPUs and counted every one.” Megaspeed denied any wrongdoing. In April, Megaspeed’s Malysisan data centre landlord terminated its contract, reallocating 68.4 megawatts of capacity to another cloud providerStay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsMoreover, Megaspeed is not the only example of how difficult it can be to police the movement of AI hardware. Earlier this year, U.S. prosecutors accused people associated with Super Micro of helping divert around $2.5 billion worth of Nvidia-powered servers to China through Southeast Asian intermediaries. The alleged scheme involved falsified paperwork and dummy server shells, with genuine hardware shipped onward after inspections. More recently, the company has faced additional scrutiny over its export compliance after inspections. Nvidia has also reportedly removed half of the Asian companies on its pre-approved buyer list and told cloud providers to keep at least 51% of their computing services with customers outside China. history.titleZh: 报道称，英伟达收紧对东南亚AI GPU的追踪，中国芯片走私引发审查
history.descriptionZh:
据报道，英伟达已要求东南亚地区的云计算服务商在申请成为官方“英伟达云合作伙伴”（NCP）时，必须注册其 Fleet Intelligence 追踪系统。彭博社称，此举旨在让英伟达多一种手段监控其 AI 加速器最终部署位置。当前美国政府对受限硬件通过区域走私网络流入中国日益不满，而东南亚被视为重要中转站。英伟达未立即置评。

NCP 资格具有实际商业价值：云服务商可获得英伟达的公开背书，并优先获得紧俏 AI 芯片供应，因此英伟达可将这些权益作为合规杠杆。知情人士称，申请 NCP 的客户现在必须加入 Fleet Intelligence。该系统对应的 Fleet Management 于去年 12 月推出，最初定位为数据中心管理工具，用于收集参与企业基础设施中英伟达硬件的部署信息，包括单个加速器的位置。这有助于英伟达判断芯片离开供应链后是否仍在预期地点运行。

技术层面，英伟达此前已开发基于软件的 GPU 追踪能力，利用 GPU 遥测数据和网络延迟测量来估算处理器运行位置。该软件被描述为由客户安装的代理程序，用于监控硬件健康、完整性和库存。其原理并非在芯片中植入硬件定位模块，而是通过客户侧软件采集运行与网络特征，推断设备所在区域。文章未披露定位精度、误差范围或支持的具体 GPU 型号等性能参数。该系统在 NCP 要求之外仍属自愿参与，英伟达也不会自动获得所有使用该软件客户的位置数据；现有 Cloud Partner 是否需要重新注册以保留资格、该要求是否会扩展到东南亚以外，均尚未明确。

这一机制的直接应用场景是出口管制合规与供应链追踪。美国限制中国企业未经许可购买先进 AI 加速器，但当局认为仍有数十亿美元硬件通过第三方网络进入中国，东南亚是重要通道。C4ADS 调查曾识别出通过研究项目、空壳公司和经其他东南亚国家转运等路线，并在 2022 至 2025 年交易中追踪到价值 1340 万美元的英伟达 A100、H100 和 AD102 系列 GPU 经区域贸易路线流动。该报告还将 46 亿美元硬件采购与总部位于新加坡的 Megaspeed International 联系起来。Megaspeed 因涉嫌芯片转移接受美国和新加坡调查已超过一年，英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋上周为其交易辩护称“完全正常”，并表示已研究其所有 GPU 部署、逐一清点；Megaspeed 否认不当行为。今年 4 月，Megaspeed 马来西亚数据中心房东终止合同，将 68.4 兆瓦容量转给另一家云服务商。

Megaspeed 并非孤例。今年早些时候，美国检方指控与 Super Micro 相关人员通过东南亚中间商，协助将约 25 亿美元英伟达服务器转运至中国，涉嫌使用伪造文件和空壳服务器，在检查后将真实硬件继续转运。此后该公司出口合规又受审查。英伟达据称已从其预批准买家名单中移除一半亚洲公司，并要求云服务商确保至少 51% 的计算服务面向中国以外客户。整体看，Fleet Intelligence 要求是英伟达将商业认证、芯片供应优先权与部署追踪绑定的一次合规创新，可能提升其对 AI 硬件流向的可见性，但也引发关于追踪范围、客户数据主权和是否向全球扩展的疑问。

history.title: Nvidia wants to repurpose over 130 old telco buildings as tiny data centers, report claims
history.description: Brightspeed has over 130 facilities located across the U.S., with Nvidia estimating that they could produce up to 1GW of compute capacity.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Internet and telecommunications provider Brightspeed is reportedly in talks with Nvidia to convert several of its buildings into tiny data centers. According to The Information, Nvidia pitched the idea to Apollo Global Management executives, the parent company of Brightspeed, who then asked it to submit written plans to the internet provider. Nvidia complied and has now requested additional information, data, and site visits to some of Brightspeed’s existing infrastructure.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleThe telecommunications company has around 130 buildings located around the country, many of which are already built to handle data and voice traffic and have the required power infrastructure to run Nvidia servers. Sources say that the AI tech giant estimates that these sites could collectively deliver around 1 gigawatt of compute capacity, which could accommodate more than 2,200 Supermicro Vera Rubin NVL72 racks containing 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs each. Although these sites already can power these GPUs, it’s still not a plug-and-play solution, as Nvidia would still need to install cooling systems and other supporting architecture. These would still require permits and approval from the local government, but they would likely face less red tape and opposition compared to building a data center from the ground up.Apollo Global Management has already made significant bets in AI hardware, with the asset management company involved in a $40 billion deal with SpaceX that would give it around 360,000 Vera Rubin GPUs across 5,000 NVL72 racks. While it’s currently unclear who will own the AI chips installed in Brightspeed facilities, the proposal could potentially help Apollo find a place for the Nvidia chips it ordered to get them up and running as soon as possible. This is a much better solution compared to waiting for years to get a data center approved, all while facing resistance from the community even after getting the go-ahead from the local government.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Having multiple small data centers like this is also a setup that OpenAI and Anthropic have been considering, especially as larger facilities are facing delays and backlash from the communities that they’re in. While having a large, homogeneous cluster built in one location is preferable for training, Nvidia representatives have described these smaller sites working together as an “inference network” to help run existing AI models. This is especially important as AI agents, which use five to ten times more tokens than humans, become more popular.The move to use existing facilities instead of building new ones from scratch has received renewed attention, especially after Americans overwhelmingly voted against data centers during the midterm elections. While the more than 300 data center bans enacted across the U.S. have only delayed three existing projects, it’s feared that the bans and moratoriums would make it that much harder to start new data center developments and make it difficult for AI companies to secure the compute capacity needed to power their AI models in the future. history.titleZh: 据报道，英伟达希望将130多栋旧电信建筑改造成小型数据中心
history.descriptionZh:
据The Information报道，美国互联网和电信提供商Brightspeed正与Nvidia洽谈，计划将旗下多栋建筑改造为小型数据中心。知情人士称，Nvidia向Brightspeed母公司Apollo Global Management的高管提出这一设想，后者要求Nvidia提交书面方案；Nvidia已照做，并进一步索取数据、补充信息，还要求实地考察Brightspeed部分现有基础设施。Brightspeed在全国约有130栋建筑，许多原本就用于承载数据和语音流量，具备运行Nvidia服务器所需的电力基础设施。Nvidia估计，这些站点合计可提供约1吉瓦算力，足以容纳超过2200个超微Vera Rubin NVL72机架；每个机架包含72颗Rubin GPU和36颗Vera CPU，按此计算约对应15.8万颗Rubin GPU和7.9万颗Vera CPU。不过，这并不是“即插即用”的方案：Nvidia仍需安装冷却系统和其他配套架构，并取得地方政府许可。相比从零新建数据中心，改造现有电信设施通常审批阻力更小、社区反对也可能更弱。

Apollo已在AI硬件领域大举下注。报道称，Apollo参与了一项与SpaceX相关的400亿美元交易，将获得约36万颗Vera Rubin GPU，分布在5000个NVL72机架中。目前尚不清楚Brightspeed设施内AI芯片的最终所有权，但该方案可能帮助Apollo为已订购的Nvidia芯片尽快找到部署地点，而不必等待多年审批和社区阻力。OpenAI和Anthropic也在考虑类似的多小型数据中心布局，因为大型吉瓦级项目面临延期和社区反弹。Nvidia代表将这种由多个小站点协同工作的模式称为“推理网络”，主要用于运行现有AI模型；训练任务仍更适合集中在单一地点的大规模同构集群。随着AI智能体普及——其token消耗量可达人类的5至10倍——分布式推理算力的重要性正在上升。这一趋势也与美国数据中心面临的政策环境有关：中期选举后，选民对数据中心反对情绪明显，全美已颁布300多项数据中心禁令，目前虽只延迟了3个现有项目，但业界担心禁令和暂停令将使新项目更难启动，并影响AI公司未来获取模型所需算力。
